Translation: As the monkey leader stood at the foot of the great mountain filled with lordly elephants he looked like an elephant standing at the centre of a pond.
Shlok: स तस्य गिरिवर्यस्य तले नागवरायुते। तिष्ठन् कपिवरस्तत्र ह्रदे नाग इवाबभौ।। (?)

Translation: Having made up his mind to leap for the cause of Rama, Hanuman began to grow in size just as the sea grows during the fullmoon and newmoon days, while the monkey troops were watching.
Shlok: प्लवङ्गप्रवरैर्दृष्टः प्लवने कृतनिश्चयः। ववृधे रामवृद्ध्यर्थं समुद्र इव पर्वसु।।
Upameya: प्लवङ्गप्रवरैर्दृष्टः (कपिवरः सः हनुमान्) from previous context

Translation: The mountain pressed hard under the feet of the valiant (Hanuman),
discharged streams of water just as an elephant in rut would exude water of intoxication.
Shlok: तेन चोत्तमवीर्येण पीड्यमानः स पर्वतः। सलिलं सम्प्रसुस्राव मदं मत्त इव द्विपः।।

Translation: The mountain pressed hard under the feet of the valiant (Hanuman),
discharged streams of water just as an elephant in rut would exude water of intoxication.
Shlok: तेन चोत्तमवीर्येण पीड्यमानः स पर्वतः। सलिलं सम्प्रसुस्राव मदं मत्त इव द्विपः।।

Translation: Hanuman the son of the Windgod, who is like a mountain, with extraordinary might intends to cross the ocean, the abode of crocodiles
Shlok: एष पर्वतसङ्काशो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। तितीर्षति महावेगस्समुद्रं मकरालयम्।।

Translation: Hanuman, huge as a mountain moved his body and shook the hair on his body, thundering like a cloud.
Shlok: दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चाचलोपमः। ननाद सुमहानादं सुमहानिव तोयदः।।

Translation: Hanuman, huge as a mountain moved his body and shook the hair on his body, thundering like a cloud.
Shlok: दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चाचलोपमः। ननाद सुमहानादं सुमहानिव तोयदः।।

Translation: Like the king of birds Garuda would shake a serpent, he shook his tail covered with hair in order to take off.
Shlok: आनुपूर्व्येण वृत्तं च लाङ्गूलं लोमभिश्चितम्। उत्पतिष्यन् विचिक्षेप पक्षिराज इवोरगम्।।

Translation: Hanuman had the tail curled at his back which appeared like a big serpent being carried off by Garuda.
Shlok: तस्य लाङ्गूलमाविद्धमात्तवेगस्य पृष्ठतः। ददृशे गरुडेनेव ह्रियमाणो महोरगः।।

Translation: Just like an arrow released by Raghava would fly, I too will proceed with the speed of the wind to reach Lanka ruled by Ravana.
Shlok: यथा राघवनिर्मुक्तः शरः श्वसनविक्रमः। गच्छेत्तद्वद्गमिष्यामि लङ्कां रावणपालिताम्।।

Translation: Swept away by the force of his thighs, the trees bent forward following him for a while just as relatives accompany their kith and kin on long travel.
Shlok: ऊरुवेगोद्धता वृक्षा मुहूर्तं कपिमन्वयुः। प्रस्थितं दीर्घमध्वानं स्वबन्धुमिव बान्धवाः।।

Translation: Uprooted by the force of Hanuman's thighs,great trees like sala followed him just like the troops follow the king.
Shlok: तमूरुवेगोन्मथिताः सालाश्चान्ये नगोत्तमाः। अनुजग्मुर्हनूमन्तं सैन्या इव महीपतिम्।।

Translation: Covered with tender sprouts and buds of different kinds of flowers Hanuman shone brightly like a flying mountain with fireflies.
Shlok: स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः। शुशुभे मेघसङ्काशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः।।

Translation: Covered with tender sprouts and buds of different kinds of flowers Hanuman shone brightly like a flying mountain with fireflies.
Shlok: स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः। शुशुभे मेघसङ्काशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः।।

Translation: Covered with tender sprouts and buds of different kinds of flowers Hanuman shone brightly like a flying mountain with fireflies.
Shlok: स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः। शुशुभे मेघसङ्काशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः।।

Translation: Covered with tender sprouts and buds of different kinds of flowers Hanuman shone brightly like a flying mountain with fireflies.
Shlok: स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः। शुशुभे मेघसङ्काशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः।।

Translation: Shedding their blossoms (under his thrust) the trees dropped into the waters of the sea just like close relatives follow at the time of farewell.
Shlok: विमुक्तास्तस्य वेगेन मुक्त्वा पुष्पाणि ते द्रुमाः। अवशीर्यन्त सलिले निवृत्ताः सुहृदो यथा।।

Translation: Covered with blossoms of different kinds and colours, Hanuman looked like a cloud brightened by lightnings in the sky.
Shlok: पुष्पौघेणानुबद्धेन नानावर्णेन वानरः। बभौ मेघ इवाकाशे विद्युद्गणविभूषितः।।

Translation: That great Vanara appeared as if he was gulping the entire ocean with its rising waves. While he was looking upward it appeared as though he was keen to drink in the sea as well.
Shlok: तस्याम्बरगतौ बाहू ददृशाते प्रसारितौ। पर्वताग्राद्विनिष्क्रान्तौ पञ्चास्याविव पन्नगौ।।

Translation: As he was moving in the sky following the direction of the wind, his eyes blazed like two fires burning on the mountain, flashing like lightning.

Shlok: तस्य विद्युत्प्रभाकारे वायुमार्गानुसारिणः। नयने विप्रकाशेते पर्वतस्थाविवानलौ।।

Translation: The large, round, reddishbrown eyes of Hanuman shed their bright light like the rising Moon and Sun.
Shlok: पिङ्गे पिङ्गाक्षमुख्यस्य बृहती परिमण्डले। चक्षुषी सम्प्राकाशेते चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ।।

Translation: By the reflection of his copperyred nose, his face looked red like the Sun's orb coming close at twilight.

Shlok: मुखं नासिकया तस्य ताम्रया ताम्रमाबभौ। सन्ध्यया समभिस्पृष्टं यथा स्यात् सूर्यमण्डलम्।।

Translation: As the son of the Windgod was flying through the sky, his coiled up tail looked splendid like the banner installed at the festival in honour of Indra (on the fifteenth day of the month of Bhadrapada).
Shlok: लाङ्गूलं च समाविद्धं प्लवमानस्य शोभते। अम्बरे वायुपुत्रस्य शक्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितम्।।

Translation: With his white teeth and curled up tail, the wise son of the Windgod looked splendid like the halo of the Sungod.
Shlok: लाङ्गूलचक्रो हनुमान् शुक्लदंष्ट्रोऽनिलात्मजः। व्यरोचत महाप्राज्ञः परिवेषीव भास्करः।।

Translation: The wind passing through the arm pits of the lionlike vanara crossing the ocean sounded like a thundering cloud.
Shlok: तस्य वानरसिंहस्य प्लवमानस्य सागरम्। कक्षान्तरगतो वायुर्जीमूत इव गर्जति।।

Translation: The elephantlike monkey was seen darting across the ocean(going from north to south) like a meteor risen in the north along with its tailend falling down the sky.
Shlok: खे यथा निपतत्युल्का ह्युत्तरान्ताद्विनिःसृता। दृश्यते सानुबन्धा च तथा स कपिकुञ्जरः।।

Translation: The vanara expanded into an enormous size form appeared as though moving like the setting Sun. He looked like a huge elephant bound round the waist.
Shlok: पतत्पतङ्गसङ्काशो व्यायतः शुशुभे कपिः। प्रवृद्ध इव मातङ्गः कक्ष्यया बध्यमानया।।

Translation: When the vanara was flying in the sky, his shadow reflected in the ocean looked like a
ship driven by the wind and sailing on the sea below (as if the lower part of his body was under water and upper part occupied the sky)
Shlok: उपरिष्टाच्छरीरेण छायया चावगाढया। सागरे मारुताविष्टा नौरिवासीत्तदा कपिः।।

Translation: The broad shadow of the son of the Windgod in the sea following him shone like a dark row of clouds sailing in the pristine sky.
Shlok: श्वेताभ्रघनराजीव वायुपुत्रानुगामिनी। तस्य सा शुशुभे छाया वितता लवणाम्भसि।।

Translation: Hanuman the great vanara, splendid with a huge body coursing through the air seemed like a winged mountain flying the sky without any support.
Shlok: शुशुभे स महातेजा महाकायो महाकपिः। वायुमार्गे निरालम्बे पक्षवानिव पर्वतः।।

Translation: Hanuman was found pulling clusters of big clouds along with him like the Windgod and appeared like Garuda,the king of birds, drawing flocks of birds along with him at the time of landing.
Shlok: आपाते पक्षिसङ्घानां पक्षिराज इव व्रजन्। हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्रकर्षन् मारुतो यथा।।

Translation: Hanuman was found pulling clusters of big clouds along with him like the Windgod and appeared like Garuda,the king of birds, drawing flocks of birds along with him at the time of landing.
Shlok: आपाते पक्षिसङ्घानां पक्षिराज इव व्रजन्। हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्रकर्षन् मारुतो यथा।।

Translation: Entering into and emerging from the clouds, he looked like the Moon that appears and disappears (behind a bank of clouds).
Shlok: प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः। प्रच्छन्नश्च प्रकाशश्च चन्द्रमा इव लक्ष्यते।।

Translation: Just as the rising Sun comes out with glowing rays tearing the veil of dark clouds, the mountain rose up from the water of the ocean.
Shlok: स सागरजलं भित्त्वा बभूवाभ्युत्थितस्तदा।।

Translation: यथा जलधरं भित्त्वा दीप्तरश्मिर्दिवाकरः।
The sky shone like barnished weapons smeared with the golden colour of the
mountain peaks that rose up above the water.
Shlok: तप्तजाम्बूनदैः शृङ्गैः पर्वतस्य समुत्थितैः। आकाशं शस्त्रसङ्काशमभवत्काञ्चनप्रभम्।।

Translation: The noble mountain, Mainaka was glittering like a thousand Suns with selfeffulgent golden peaks shining.
Shlok: जातरूपमयैः शृङ्गैर्भ्राजमानैः स्वयंप्रभैः। आदित्यशतसङ्काशः सोऽभवद्गिरिसत्तमः।।(?)

Translation: The great vanara,who was swift in action felled down the mountain that had risen high instantly with his chest just as the wind would strike a cloud.
Shlok: स तमुच्छ्र्रतमत्यर्थं महावेगो महाकपिः। उरसा पातयामास जीमूतमिव मारुतः।।

Translation: The great vanara,who was swift in action felled down the mountain that had risen high instantly with his chest just as the wind would strike a cloud.
Shlok: स तमुच्छ्र्रतमत्यर्थं महावेगो महाकपिः। उरसा पातयामास जीमूतमिव मारुतः।।

Translation: O foremost among the vanaras you are the son of the highsouled Windgod's, preeminent among the gods, you are also equal to him in speed.
Shlok: त्वं हि देववरिष्ठस्य मारुतस्य महात्मनः।

Translation: पुत्रस्तस्यैव वेगेन सदृशः कपिकुञ्जर।।
Then the gods, gandharvas, siddhas and great sages approached Surasa, the mother of nagas, who was glowing like the Sungod and said
Shlok: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। अब्रुवन् सूर्यसङ्काशां सुरसां नागमातरम्।।

Translation: The glorious son of the Windgod, called Hanuman, is crossing the ocean. Obstruct him for sometime by assuming the hideous form of a demon, gigantic as a mountain, fearful with yellowishbrown eyes, with big teeth and a wide mouth like the sky.
Shlok: राक्षसं रूपमास्थाय सुघोरं पर्वतोपमम्। दंष्ट्राकरालं पिङ्गाक्षं वक्त्रं कृत्वा नभः समम्।। (स्पृशम्)

Translation: Seeing Hanuman released out of her mouth like the Moon released from the mouth of Rahu, Surasa assumed her true form and said
Shlok: तं दृष्ट्वा वदनान्मुक्तं चन्द्रं राहुमुखादिव। अब्रवीत्सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण वानरम्।।

Translation: Rising above the invincible ocean, the abode of lord Varuna, Hanuman coursed through the sky speedily like Garuda.
Shlok: स सागरमनाधृष्यमभ्येत्य वरुणालयम्। जगामाकाशमाविश्य वेगेन गरुडोपमः।।

Translation: Hanuman, son of the Windgod was seen everywhere in the sky. He appeared like a
longwinged king of mountains unsupported.
Shlok: प्रदृश्यमानः सर्वत्रः हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः। भेजेऽम्बरं निरालम्बं लम्बपक्ष इवाद्रिराट्।।

Translation: I am caught suddenly. I am handicapped.I am like a huge ship in an ocean retarded by the wind blowing from the opposite direction.
Shlok: समाक्षिप्तोऽस्मि सहसा पङ्गूकृतपराक्रमः। प्रतिलोमेन वातेन महानौरिव सागरे।।

Translation: Recognising the true nature of Simhika the clutcher of shadows, the wise Hanuman grew to a huge size like a cloud in rainy season.
Shlok: स तां बुद्ध्वार्थतत्त्वेन सिंहिकां मतिमान्कपिः। व्यवर्धत महाकायः प्रावृषीव वलाहकः।।

Translation: Observing the body of Hanuman growing in size, Simhika started distending her mouth wide like the depth of the underworld.
Shlok: तस्य सा कायमुद्वीक्ष्य वर्धमानं महाकपेः। वक्त्रं प्रसारयामास पातालान्तरसन्निभम्।।
घनराजीव गर्जन्ती वानरं समभिद्रवत्। स ददर्श ततस्तस्या विवृतं सुमहन्मुखम्।।

Translation: Siddhas and Caranas beheld him disappearing into her mouth like the full moon being devoured on a full moon night by the demon Rāhu.
Shlok: आस्ये तस्या निमज्जन्तं ददृशुः सिद्धचारणाः। ग्रस्यमानं यथा चन्द्रं पूर्णं पर्वणि राहुणा।।

Translation: O lord of vanaras he in whom these four qualities, fortitude, vision, intelligence and dexterity exist as in you will achieve his mission and not get lost
Shlok: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्यं सः कर्मसु न सीदति।।

Translation: Looking at the ocean, he observed the sea bordering the land and the trees grown on the marshy land in the region of the mouths of the rivers (the consorts of the sea.). Looking at his own body which was like a huge cloud as though obstructing the sky, the wise monkey of selfcontrol thought as follows.
Shlok: स तैः सम्भावितः पूज्यः प्रतिपन्नप्रयोजनः। जगामाकाशमाविश्य पन्नगाशनवत्कपिः।।

Translation: Looking at the ocean, he observed the sea bordering the land and the trees grown on the marshy land in the region of the mouths of the rivers (the consorts of the sea.). Looking at his own body which was like a huge cloud as though obstructing the sky, the wise monkey of selfcontrol thought as follows.
Shlok: स महामेघसङ्काशं समीक्ष्यात्मानमात्मवान्। निरुन्धन्तमिवाकाशं चकार मतिमान् मतिम्।।

Translation: Then Hanuman contracted his huge mountainlike body and assumed his normal form, just as a sage who gives up ignorance on awakening .
Shlok: ततः शरीरं संक्षिप्य तन्महीधरसन्निभम्। पुनः प्रकृतिमापेदे वीतमोह इवात्मवान्।।

Translation: Then Hanuman contracted his huge mountainlike body and assumed his normal form, just as a sage who gives up ignorance on awakening .
Shlok: ततः शरीरं संक्षिप्य तन्महीधरसन्निभम्। पुनः प्रकृतिमापेदे वीतमोह इवात्मवान्।।

Translation: Hanuman returned to his normal form contracting to his small size, just like Lord Visnu returned to his original form after taking three strides and defeating the valour of king Bali.
Shlok: तद्रूपमतिसंक्षिप्य हनुमान् प्रकृतौ स्थितः। त्रीन् क्रमानिव विक्रम्य बलिवीर्यहरो हरिः।।

Translation: The heroic vanara saw the rising Moon flitting in and out shining like a fresh white conch, in the colour of milk and lotus stalks, bright like a swan floating in the lakelike sky.
Shlok: शङ्खप्रभं क्षीरमृणालवर्णमुद्गच्छमानं व्यवभासमानम्। ददर्श चन्द्रं स हरिप्रवीरः पोप्लूयमानं सरसीव हंसम्।।

Translation: The mighty son of the Windgod, intelligent Hanuman, an elephant among vanaras, standing on the peak of the Lamba which looked like a high rainbearing cloud and relying on his energy, entered by night the city of Lanka, ruled by Ravana rich in delightful forests, groves and water pools.
Shlok: स लम्बशिखरे लम्बे लम्बतोयदसन्निभे। सत्त्वमास्थाय मेधावी हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।।

Translation: Hanuman looked at the city of the demon king, whose darkness was dispelled by bright gems and mighty mansions as if it were a young maiden. The prosperous city was like a well decorated woman, adorned with ornaments having walls for her dress, the stables for her earrings, the armouries for her breasts. (उपमेय??)
Shlok: तां रत्नवसनोपेतां कोष्ठागारावतंसकाम्। यन्त्रागारस्तनीमृद्धां प्रमदामिव भूषिताम्।। तां नष्टतिमिरां दीप्तैर्भास्वरैश्च महागृहैः। नगरीं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य स ददर्श महाकपिः।।5.3.19।।

Translation: On hearing the words of ogress of Lanka, the son of the Windgod stood up ready and appeared like another mountain.
Shlok: लङ्काया वचनं श्रुत्वा हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। यत्नवान्स हरिश्रेष्ठः स्थितश्शैल इवापरः।।(?)

Translation: The delightful city looked charming with its excellent houses, which resounded with exquisite peals of laughter preceded by the sound of musical instruments, were marked with figures of thunderbolts and goads and adorned with lattice-windows of diamonds, even as the sky looks charming with clouds. (6)
Shlok: वज्राङ्कुशनिकाशैश्च वज्रजालविभूषितैः ।  गृहमेघैः पुरी रम्या बभासे द्यौरिवाम्बुदैः ॥ ६ ॥

Translation: The delightful city looked charming with its excellent houses, which resounded with exquisite peals of laughter preceded by the sound of musical instruments, were marked with figures of thunderbolts and goads and adorned with lattice-windows of diamonds, even as the sky looks charming with clouds. (6)
Shlok: वज्राङ्कुशनिकाशैश्च वज्रजालविभूषितैः ।  गृहमेघैः पुरी रम्या बभासे द्यौरिवाम्बुदैः ॥ ६ ॥

Translation: The city of Lanka appeared radiant with its tall mansions resembling white clouds. The mansions had auspicious marks of lotus and swastika engraved on them and were opening in the direction of the south.
Shlok: प्रजज्वाल ततो लङ्का रक्षोगणगृहैः शुभैः। सिताभ्रसदृशैश्चित्रैः पद्मस्वस्तिकसंस्थितैः।।

Translation: Then intelligent Hanuman observed the Moon in the central part of the sky spreading a canopy of his luminescence like the Sun, and looking like an intoxicated mighty (white) bull moving in a stable.
Shlok: ततः स मध्यंगतमंशुमन्तं ज्योत्स्नावितानं महदुद्वमन्तम्।

Translation: ददर्श धीमान् दिवि भानुमन्तं गोष्ठे वृषं मत्तमिव भ्रमन्तम्।।
Like a swan in a cage of silver, like a lion in a cave of Mandara mountain, like a hero on a proud, intoxicated elephant, the Moon shone in the sky.
Shlok: हंसो यथा राजतपञ्जरस्थः सिंहो यथा मन्दरकन्दरस्थः।

Translation: वीरो यथा गर्वितकुञ्जरस्थ चन्द्रोऽपि बभ्राज तथाम्बरस्थः।।
The fullmoon with its hornlike spot shone like a bull with sharp horns, like the white Himalayan mountain with its lofty peaks, and like an elephant with gold plated tusks
Shlok: स्थितः ककुद्मानिव तीक्ष्णशृङ्गो महाचलः श्वेत इवोच्चशृङ्गः। हस्तीव जाम्बूनदबद्धशृङ्गो रराज चन्द्रः परिपूर्णशृङ्गः।।

Translation: The fullmoon with its hornlike spot shone like a bull with sharp horns, like the white Himalayan mountain with its lofty peaks, and like an elephant with gold plated tusks
Shlok: स्थितः ककुद्मानिव तीक्ष्णशृङ्गो महाचलः श्वेत इवोच्चशृङ्गः। हस्तीव जाम्बूनदबद्धशृङ्गो रराज चन्द्रः परिपूर्णशृङ्गः।।

Translation: The fullmoon with its hornlike spot shone like a bull with sharp horns, like the white Himalayan mountain with its lofty peaks, and like an elephant with gold plated tusks
Shlok: स्थितः ककुद्मानिव तीक्ष्णशृङ्गो महाचलः श्वेत इवोच्चशृङ्गः। हस्तीव जाम्बूनदबद्धशृङ्गो रराज चन्द्रः परिपूर्णशृङ्गः।।

Translation: The Moon shone bright like a lion mounted on a rock, like a lordly elephant in a deep forest, like a king on attaining the kingdom.
Shlok: शिलातलं प्राप्य यथा मृगेन्द्रो महारणं प्राप्य यथा गजेन्द्रः। राज्यं समासाद्य यथा नरेन्द्रस्तथा प्रकाशो विरराज चन्द्रः।।

Translation: The Moon shone bright like a lion mounted on a rock, like a lordly elephant in a deep forest, like a king on attaining the kingdom.
Shlok: शिलातलं प्राप्य यथा मृगेन्द्रो महारणं प्राप्य यथा गजेन्द्रः। राज्यं समासाद्य यथा नरेन्द्रस्तथा प्रकाशो विरराज चन्द्रः।।

Translation: The Moon shone bright like a lion mounted on a rock, like a lordly elephant in a deep forest, like a king on attaining the kingdom.
Shlok: शिलातलं प्राप्य यथा मृगेन्द्रो महारणं प्राप्य यथा गजेन्द्रः। राज्यं समासाद्य यथा नरेन्द्रस्तथा प्रकाशो विरराज चन्द्रः।।

Translation: There he saw demonesses adorned with choicest ornaments, their minds attached faithfully to their husbands and bottles of wine. Some of the wives of the demons, however, looked gentle and bright like stars.
Shlok: ततो वरार्हाः सुविशुद्धभावा स्तेषां स्त्रियस्तत्र महानुभावाः।

Translation: प्रियेषु पानेषु च सक्तभावा ददर्श तारा इव सुप्रभावाः।।

There he saw cheerful demonesses shining brightly, abashed by the embrace of their beloveds during the night. He also saw those sporting with their beloveds freely and looking like birds embracing flowers. (recheck)
Shlok: श्रिया ज्वलन्तीस्त्रपयोपगूढा निशीथकाले रमणोपगूढाः।

Translation: ददर्श काश्चित्प्रमदोपगूढा यथा विहङ्गाः कुसुमोपगूढाः।।
Ogresses without veil, some altruistic, some separated from their husbands looked pale like the Moon, though possessed of polished gold complexion.
Shlok: अप्रावृताः काञ्चनराजिवर्णाः काश्चित्परार्थ्यास्तपनीयवर्णाः।

Translation: पुनश्च काश्चिच्छशलक्ष्मवर्णाः कान्तप्रहीणा रुचिराङ्गवर्णाः।।
Hanuman could not find Sita anywhere, an excellent lady born in a noble royal family, adopting the right path, a lady delicate like a blossoming creeper of good breed, or so he imagined.
Shlok: न त्वेव सीतां परमाभिजातां पथि स्थिते राजकुले प्रजाताम्।

Translation: लतां प्रपुल्लामिव साधु जातां ददर्श तन्वीं मनसाभिजाताम्।।

She would be like a barely visible ray of the Moon, like a streak of gold covered with dust, like an unhealed scar of a wound caused by an arrow only superficially covered and like a flake of cloud swept off by the wind.
Shlok: अव्यक्तरेखामिव चन्द्ररेखां पांसुप्रदिग्धामिव हेमरेखाम्।

Translation: क्षतप्ररूढामिव बाणरेखां वायुप्रभिन्नामिव मेघरेखाम्।।
Then he reached the residence of the lord of demons enclosed by a red colour compound wall dazzling like the midday Sun.
Shlok: आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान्राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्।

Translation: प्राकारेणार्कवर्णेन भास्वरेणाभिसम्वृतम्।।
The elephant among vanaras (Hanuman), scanned the mansion defended by dreadful demons like a forest protected by lions.
Shlok: रक्षितं राक्षसैर्घोरैः सिंहैरिव महद्वनम्।

Translation: समीक्षमाणो भवनं चकाशे कपिकुञ्जरः।।
The elephant among vanaras (Hanuman), scanned the mansion defended by dreadful demons like a forest protected by lions.
Shlok: रक्षितं राक्षसैर्घोरैः सिंहैरिव महद्वनम्। समीक्षमाणो भवनं चकाशे कपिकुञ्जरः।।

Translation: Full of the jewels of joyous women, the residence of the lord of demons reverberated with the jingling of their ornaments and accessories like the sound of the sea.

Shlok: मुदितप्रमदारत्नं राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्। वराभरणसंह्रादैः समुद्रस्वनन्निस्वनम्।।

Translation: The place was full of eminent demons with royal traits like a dense forest infested with lions. It carried the fragrance of agaru and sandal of good quality.
Shlok: तद्राजगुणसम्पन्नं मुख्यैश्चागुरुचन्दनैः। महाजनैः समाकीर्णं सिंहैरिव महद्वनम्।।

Translation: The place was full of eminent demons with royal traits like a dense forest infested with lions. It carried the fragrance of agaru and sandal of good quality.
Shlok: तद्राजगुणसम्पन्नं मुख्यैश्चागुरुचन्दनैः। महाजनैः समाकीर्णं सिंहैरिव महद्वनम्।।

Translation: The place produced deep sounds like the sea. Those mighty ogres wore gemstudded ornaments. The great vanara saw the residence of the great self, Ravana rich with precious gems.
Shlok: समुद्रमिव गम्भीरं समुद्रमिव निस्स्वनम्। महात्मनो महद् वेश्म महारत्नपरिच्छदम्।।

Translation: Then the great vanara leaped from the residence of Kumbhakarna which looked like a cloud to Vibhishana's.
Shlok: अथ मेघप्रतीकाशं कुम्भकर्णनिवेशनम्।

Translation: विभीषणस्य च तदा पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः।।
He saw in the palace of Ravana, the demon king, thousands of troops adorned with gold, fully protected with armour of gold shining like the morning Sun.
Shlok: सहस्रं वाहिनीस्तत्र जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताः।।5.6.34।। हेमजालपरिच्छन्नास्तरुणादित्यसन्निभाः। ददर्श राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य निवेशने।।

Translation: The palace of Ravana looked splendid with gems of different hues and with Ravana's presence, it was shining like the radiant Sungod
Shlok: अर्चिर्भिश्चापि रत्नानां तेजसा रावणस्य च। विरराजाथ तद्वेश्म रश्मिमानिव रश्मिभिः।।

Translation: The palace of Ravana looked splendid with gems of different hues and with Ravana's presence, it was shining like the radiant Sungod
Shlok: अर्चिर्भिश्चापि रत्नानां तेजसा रावणस्य च। विरराजाथ तद्वेश्म रश्मिमानिव रश्मिभिः।।

Translation: Powerful Hanuman beheld the conglomeration of buildings with golden lattices encrusted with vaidurya, with flocks of birds comparable to a complex of clouds pierced by lightning during rainy season.
Shlok: स वेश्मजालं बलवान् ददर्श व्यासक्तवैडूर्यसुवर्णजालम्। यथा महत्प्रावृषि मेघजालं विद्युत्पिनद्धं सविहङ्गजालम्।।

Translation: Powerful Hanuman beheld the conglomeration of buildings with golden lattices encrusted with vaidurya, with flocks of birds comparable to a complex of clouds pierced by lightning during rainy season.
Shlok: स वेश्मजालं बलवान् ददर्श व्यासक्तवैडूर्यसुवर्णजालम्। यथा महत्प्रावृषि मेघजालं विद्युत्पिनद्धं सविहङ्गजालम्।।

Translation: Powerful Hanuman beheld the conglomeration of buildings with golden lattices encrusted with vaidurya, with flocks of birds comparable to a complex of clouds pierced by lightning during rainy season.
Shlok: स वेश्मजालं बलवान् ददर्श व्यासक्तवैडूर्यसुवर्णजालम्। यथा महत्प्रावृषि मेघजालं विद्युत्पिनद्धं सविहङ्गजालम्।।

Translation: It appeared splendid like a scattered piece of heaven on earth, glittering with countless gems. It looked like a mountain peak covered with pollen of flowers dropped from all kinds of trees.
Shlok: ततो ददर्शोच्छ्रितमेघरूपं मनोहरं काञ्चनचारुरूपम् । रक्षोऽधिपस्यात्मबलानुरूपं गृहोत्तमं ह्यप्रतिरूपरूपम् ।। ५ । महीतले स्वर्गमिव प्रकीर्णं श्रिया ज्वलन्तं बहुरत्नकीर्णम्। नानातरूणां कुसुमावकीर्णं गिरेरिवाग्रं रजसावकीर्णम्।।

Translation: A jewel among aerial chariots, it looked colourful with many gems beset. It appeared like the summit of a mountain decorated with the colours of minerals, like the sky bespangled with planets and the Moon and like a mass of multicoloured clouds adorned by a rainbow.
Shlok: यथा नगाग्रं बहुधातुचित्रं यथा नभश्च ग्रहचन्द्रचित्रम्। ददर्श युक्तीकृतमेघचित्रं विमानरत्नं बहुरत्नचित्रम्।।

Translation: A jewel among aerial chariots, it looked colourful with many gems beset. It appeared like the summit of a mountain decorated with the colours of minerals, like the sky bespangled with planets and the Moon and like a mass of multicoloured clouds adorned by a rainbow.
Shlok: यथा नगाग्रं बहुधातुचित्रं यथा नभश्च ग्रहचन्द्रचित्रम्। ददर्श युक्तीकृतमेघचित्रं विमानरत्नं बहुरत्नचित्रम्।।

Translation: The immeasurable Pushpaka fashioned by Visvakarma with images of incomparable beauty was not possible to describe.  An excellent product of his achievement, it was placed in the aerial path appearing as a beaconlight (signpost) in the orbit of the Sun.
Shlok: तदप्रमेयाप्रतिकारकृत्रिमं कृतं स्वयं साध्विति विश्वकर्मणा। दिवं गतं वायुपथप्रतिष्ठितं व्यराजतादित्यपथस्य लक्ष्मवत्।।

Translation: The Pushpaka was specially designed in a unique manner. It was decorated with many colourful peaks. It was delghtful and pleasing to the mind and bright like the autumnal fullmoon. It looked like a mountain with many wonderful towers around.
Shlok: विशेषमालम्ब्य विशेषसंस्थितं

Translation: विचित्रकूटं बहुकूटमण्डितम्।
मनोऽभिरामं शरदिन्दुनिर्मलं
विचित्रकूटं शिखरं गिरेर्यथा।।
It was well built by Visvakarma and and had golden stairways, with radiant platforms glowing like fire and Sun.
Shlok: ज्वलनार्कप्रतीकाशं सुकृतं विश्वकर्मणा।

Translation: हेमसोपानसंयुक्तं चारुप्रवरवेदिकम्।।
It was bright like molten gold, fragrant with red sandal comparable to the rising Sun.
Shlok: चन्दनेन च रक्तेन तपनीयनिभेन च।

Translation: सुपुण्यगन्धिना युक्तमादित्यतरुणोपमम्।।
It was bright like molten gold, fragrant with red sandal comparable to the rising Sun.
Shlok: चन्दनेन च रक्तेन तपनीयनिभेन च।

Translation: सुपुण्यगन्धिना युक्तमादित्यतरुणोपमम्।।
Then he proceeded to an auspicious hall, which was Ravana's favourite like his chief queen dear to his heart.
Shlok: ततस्तां प्रस्थितश्शालां ददर्श महतीं शुभाम्। रावणस्य मनः कान्तां कान्तामिव वरस्त्रियम्।।
महत्या कुथयास्तीर्णां पृथिवीलक्षणाङ्कया। पृथिवीमिव विस्तीर्णां सराष्ट्रगृहमालिनीम्।।

Translation: It was smoky with fumes of agaru incence though spotless like a swan. It was colourful and radiant like Kamadhenu, the wishfulfilling cow, because of the offering of flowers.
Shlok: धूम्रामगरुधूपेन विमलां हंसपाण्डुराम्। चित्रां पुष्पोपहारेण कल्माषीमिव सुप्रभाम्।।

Translation: The chamber of Ravana, like a mother, gratified all the five senses of Hanuman with proper objects of the senses.
Shlok: इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थैस्तु पञ्च पञ्चभिरुत्तमैः।

Translation: तर्पयामास मातेव तदा रावणपालिता।।
Seeing the golden lamps that stood burning steadily, Hanuman thought they looked like gamblers in deep thought defeated by expert gamblers in a game of dice.

Shlok: प्रध्यायत इवापश्यत्प्रदीपांस्तत्र काञ्चनान्। धूर्तानिव महाधूतैर्देवनेन पराजितान्।।

Translation: Fast asleep, sounds of their ornaments silenced, the young women looked like a large bed of lotuses with swans and bees sitting calm without their usual noise.
Shlok: तत्प्रसुप्तं विरुरुचे निश्शब्दान्तरभूषणम्। निःशब्दहंसभ्रमरं यथा पद्मवनं महत्।।

Translation: The floor was covered with a wide carpet spread from wall to wall with designs of different murals of many places and houses drawn in a row (garland like). The big carpet appeared like the expanse of earth itself.
Shlok: महत्या कुथयास्तीर्णां पृथिवीलक्षणाङ्कया।

Translation: पृथिवीमिव विस्तीर्णां सराष्ट्रगृहमालिनीम्।।
The intoxicated bees would again and again long to enjoy these beautiful faces which were like blooming lotuses.
Shlok: इमानि मुखपद्मानि नियतं मत्तषट्पदाः।

Translation: अम्बुजानीव फुल्लानि प्रार्थयन्ति पुनः पुनः।।
Brightened by (the beauty of) the maidens, the mansion shone like the autumnal sky endearing and pleasing with stars.
Shlok: सा तस्य शुशुभे शाला ताभिस्त्रीभिर्विराजिता। शारदीव प्रसन्ना द्यौस्ताराभिरभिशोभिता।।

Translation: The lord of demons surrounded by women shone like the beautiful Moon encircled by stars.
Shlok: स च ताभिः परिवृतः शुशुभे राक्षसाधिपः ।  यथा ह्युडुपतिः श्रीमांस्ताराभिरिव संवृतः ॥ ४१ ॥

Translation: It was clear that the grace and lustre of those women looked brilliant like the lustre and grace of brilliant stars releasing an auspicious glow.
Shlok: ताराणामिव सुव्यक्तं महतीनां शुभार्चिषाम्। प्रभावर्णप्रसादाश्च विरेजुस्तत्र योषिताम्।।

Translation: With their good eartops broken and flower garlands crushed some looked like blooming creepers in a dense forest crushed by mighty elephants.
Shlok: सुकुण्डलधराश्चान्या विच्छिन्नमृदितस्रजः। गजेन्द्रमृदिताः फुल्ला लता इव महावने।।

Translation: The pearl chains, large and shining like rays of the Moon in the space between the breasts looked like sleeping swans.
Shlok: चन्द्रांशुकिरणाभाश्च हाराः कासांचिदुत्कटाः। हंसा इव बभुस्सुप्ताः स्तनमध्येषु योषिताम्।।

Translation: Their hips were like river banks crowded with swans, karandava and Chakravaka birds shining like rivers.
Shlok: हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः। आपगा इव ता रेजुर्जघनैः पुलिनैरिव।।

Translation: With their tiny bells round their girdle looking like buds, the bold golden ornaments like lotuses, their gestures of love like crocodiles and their radiant beauty like silver banks, the women looked like smoky rivers.
Shlok: किङ्किणीजालसङ्कोशास्ता हैमविपुलाम्बुजाः।

Translation: भावग्राहा यशस्तीराः सुप्ता नद्य इवाऽऽबभुः।।
The beautiful imprints made by the (heavy) ornaments on the tender limbs, breasts and nipples of some women appeared like many ornaments.
Shlok: मृदुष्वङ्गेषु कासाञ्चित्कुचाग्रेषु च संस्थिताः। बभुर्वर्भूषणानीव शुभा भूषणराजयः।।

Translation: The fringes of their garments glowing beautifully close to the faces of the wives (of Ravana) with different beautiful hues, shone splendid like flags.
Shlok: ताः पताका इवोद्धूताः पत्नीनां रुचिरप्रभाः। नानावर्णसुवर्णानां वक्त्रमूलेषु रेजिरे।।

Translation: Knit with the shoulders of one another like a garland of flowers intertwined with the tipsy bees resting the women shone.
Shlok: अन्योन्यभुजसूत्रेण स्त्रीमाला ग्रथिता हि सा। मालेव ग्रथिता सूत्रे शुशुभे मत्तषट्पदा।।

Translation: Hanuman saw an umbrella in one spot decorated with the best of garlands. The white umbrella looked like the Moon, lord of stars.
Shlok: तस्य चैकतमे देशे दिव्यमालोपशोभितम् । ददर्श पाण्डुरं छत्रं ताराधिपतिसंनिभम् ॥

Translation: He saw an exquisite couch made of gold shining wonderfully like the Sun. It was decorated with ashoka flowers.
Shlok: जातरूपपरिक्षिप्तं चित्रभानोः समप्रभम् ।  अशोकमालाविततं ददर्श परमासनम् ॥ ४ ॥

Translation: Hanuman saw the mightyarmed, heroic lord of demons, sleeping with huge bloodshot eyes looking like a cloud, he was adorned with flashing earrings, and clad in robes of silver texture.
Shlok: तस्मिन् जीमूतसंकाशं प्रदीप्तोत्तमकुण्डलम्।

Translation: लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुं महारजतवाससम्।।

he looked like a cloud reddened by twilight and flashing with the lightning of his ornaments. He was handsome and could assume any form at will. He looked like Mandara mountain surrounded thickly with trees and wild bushes
Shlok: वृतमाभरणैर्दिव्यैः सुरूपं कामरूपिणम्।

Translation: सवृक्षवनगुल्माढ्यं प्रसुप्तमिव मन्दरम्।।
Having reached Ravana, who was breathing (hissing) like a snake, Hanuman was for a moment frightened and drew away from him as if he was put to terrible fear.
Shlok: निःश्वसन्तं यथा नागं रावणं वानरोत्तमः ।  आसाद्य परमोद्विग्नः सोपासर्पत् सुभीतवत् ॥ १२ ॥

Translation: While the lord of demons lay asleep on the magnificent couch, he looked like the Prasravana hill with its elephant in rut.
Shlok: शुशुभे राक्षसेन्द्रस्य स्वपतः शयनोत्तमम्। गन्धहस्तिनि संविष्टे यथा प्रस्रवणं महत्।।

Translation: The vanara, gazed at the arms of Ravana placed on the couch that appeared like two angry snakes asleep in a cave on (the lap) of mount Mandara.
Shlok: ददर्श स कपिस्तत्र बाहू शयनसंस्थितौ। मन्दरस्यांतरे सुप्तौ महाही रुषिताविव।।

Translation: The lord of demons looked splendid like a mountain with his long, fully developed arms. He appeared like Mandara mountain with two lofty peaks.
Shlok: ताभ्यां स परिपूर्णाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां राक्षसेश्वरः। शुशुभेऽचलसङ्काशः शृङ्गाभ्यामिव मन्दरः।।
माषराशिप्रतीकाशं निश्श्वसन्तं भुजङ्गवत्। गाङ्गे महति तोयान्ते प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।
माषराशिप्रतीकाशं निश्श्वसन्तं भुजङ्गवत्। गाङ्गे महति तोयान्ते प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।
माषराशिप्रतीकाशं निश्श्वसन्तं भुजङ्गवत्। गाङ्गे महति तोयान्ते प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।
चतुर्भिः काञ्चनैर्दीपैर्दीप्यमानं चतुर्दिशम् । प्रकाशीकृतसर्वांगं मेघं विद्युद्गणैरिव ॥ २९ ॥

Translation: There the beautiful moonlike faces of women Illumined by the lovely earrings lay on the cot which looked resplendent like the sky lit up with hosts of stars.
Shlok: तासां चन्द्रोपमैर्वक्त्रैश्शुभैर्ललितकुण्डलैः। विरराज विमानं तन्नभस्तारागणैरिव।।

Translation: There the beautiful moonlike faces of women Illumined by the lovely earrings lay on the cot which looked resplendent like the sky lit up with hosts of stars. (Rethink second pair of Upama)
Shlok: तासां चन्द्रोपमैर्वक्त्रैश्शुभैर्ललितकुण्डलैः। विरराज विमानं तन्नभस्तारागणैरिव।।

Translation: Another woman slept hugging her veena. She shone like a lotus plant flung in a large river, clinging on to a boat. (Veena is compared to a boat and the woman to a lotusplant in the ambience of flowing waters of the river. The entire hall had put up such a dynamic view showing hectic life of the inmates).
Shlok: काचिद्वीणां परिष्वज्य प्रसुप्ता सम्प्रकाशते। महानदीप्रकीर्णेव नलिनी पोतमाश्रिता।।

Translation: A woman with dark eyes asleep with a drum placed in her armpit looked like a beautiful mother holding her loving baby (the drum was hung to her arm with a rope). उत्प्रेक्षा??
Shlok: अन्या कक्षगतेनैव मड्डुकेनासितेक्षणा। प्रसुप्ता भामिनी भाति बालपुत्रेव वत्सला।।

Translation: Another selfpossessed lady, graceful in dance, holding a sevenstringed lute was as though lying asleep with her beloved.
Shlok: विपञ्चीं परिगृह्यान्या नियता नृत्तशालिनी।

Translation: निद्रावशमनुप्राप्ता सह कान्तेव भामिनी।।
One lovely woman and another held a drum and slept as if they were hugging their young child.
Shlok: डिण्डिमं परिगृह्यान्या तथैवासक्तडिण्डिमा। प्रसुप्ता तरुणं वत्समुपगूह्येव भामिनी।।

Translation: In the midst of these women the longarmed lord of demons shone like a (majestic) bull in a big cowshed.
Shlok: तासां मध्ये महाबाहुः शुशुभे राक्षसेश्वरः।

Translation: गोष्ठे महति मुख्यानां गवां मध्ये यथा वृषः।।
In the midst of these women the longarmed lord of demons shone like a (majestic) bull in a big cowshed.
Shlok: तासां मध्ये महाबाहुः शुशुभे राक्षसेश्वरः। गोष्ठे महति मुख्यानां गवां मध्ये यथा वृषः।।

Translation: Surrounded by the women, the demon king shone like a proud elephant attended by many female elephants scattered in a dense forest.
Shlok: स राक्षसेन्द्रः शुशुभे ताभिः परिवृतस्स्वयम्। करेणुभिर्यथाऽरण्ये परिकीर्णो महाद्विपः।।

Translation: Surrounded by the women, the demon king shone like a proud elephant attended by many female elephants scattered in a dense forest.
Shlok: स राक्षसेन्द्रः शुशुभे ताभिः परिवृतस्स्वयम्। करेणुभिर्यथाऽरण्ये परिकीर्णो महाद्विपः।।

Translation: The lovely clothes and garlands on the bodies of women were moving mildly by their exhalations as if shaken by the gentle breeze. (Doubtful!!)
Shlok: तासामुच्छवासवातेन वस्त्रं माल्यं च गात्रजम्।

Translation: नात्यर्थं स्पन्दते चित्रं प्राप्य मन्दमिवानिलम्।।
Withered due to indulgence in sex they were overcome with sleep. The charm of the women was like the lotus creepers with closed lotuses .
Shlok: काश्चित् काञ्चनवर्णाङ्ग्यः प्रमदा राक्षसालये। तासां निद्रावशत्वाच्च मदनेन विमूर्छितम्।।
काश्चित् काञ्चनवर्णाङ्ग्यः प्रमदा राक्षसालये। तासां निद्रावशत्वाच्च मदनेन विमूर्छितम्।।

Translation: Hanuman, the vanara leader, jumped from the aerial chariot to the boundary wall like a flash of lightning in the clouds.
Shlok: विमानात्तु सुसम्क्रम्य प्राकारं हरियूथपः।

Translation: हनुमान्वेगवानासीद्यथा विद्युद्घनान्तरे।।
Or, I think Sita might have been imprisoned in a cage like a myna in Ravana's palace. She will be surely crying.
Shlok: अथवा निहिता मन्ये रावणस्य निवेशने। नूनं लालप्यते सीता पञ्जरस्थेव शारिका।।

Translation: Or else, I shall carry him across the sea and put him before Rama like a bull as if he is a sacrificial prey to lord Siva.
Shlok: अथवैनं समुत्क्षिप्य उपर्युपरि सागरम्। रामायोपहरिष्यामि पशुं पशुपतेरिव।।

Translation: He penetrated like an arrow released from a bow the cluster of trees covering mango grove and overgrown with hundreds of creepers.
Shlok: अथाम्रवणसञ्छन्नां लताशतसमावृताम्।

Translation: ज्यामुक्त इव नाराचः पुप्लुवे वृक्षवाटिकाम्।।
Covered with flowers, Hanuman shone like a mountain of flowers in the midst of Ashoka grove.
Shlok: पुष्पावकीर्णश्शुशुभे हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। अशोकवनिकामध्ये यथा पुष्पमयो गिरिः।।

Translation: Strewn with flowers of various colours fallen from the trees of various kinds, the goddess of earth looked charming like a young woman profusely bedecked.
Shlok: वृक्षेभ्यः पतितैः पुष्पैरवकीर्णा पृथग्विधैः । रराज वसुधा तत्र प्रमदेव विभूषिता ॥ १३ ॥

Translation: The tree tops, shorn of their leaves and flowers and fruits fallen, appeared like gamblers who had lost their stakes and had to lay down their clothes and ornaments.
Shlok: निर्धूतपत्रशिखराः शीर्णपुष्पफला द्रुमाः। निक्षिप्तवस्त्राभरणा धूर्ता इव पराजिताः।।

Translation: The garden of Ashoka with trees shattered and crushed by Hanuman's tail, hands and feet, appeared like a woman with dishevelled hair, with her vermilion mark effaced, her bright teeth and lips faded for being kissed and wounded with nails and bitten with teeth (by her lover).
Shlok: विधूतकेशी युवतिर्यथा मृदितवर्णका । निपीतशुभदन्तोष्ठी नखैर्दन्तैश्च विक्षता ॥ १८ ॥ तथा लांगूलहस्तैस्तु चरणाभ्यां च मर्दिता । तथैवाशोकवनिका प्रभग्नवनपादपा ॥ १९ ॥
Upameya: लांगूलहस्तैस्तु चरणाभ्यां च मर्दिता प्रभग्नवनपादपा अशोकवनिका
Upamāna: विधूतकेशी , मृदितवर्णका, निपीतशुभदन्तोष्ठी नखैर्दन्तैश्च विक्षता युवतिः

Translation: Hanuman shook with tremendous speed the huge clusters of creepers hanging there just like stormy wind in rainy season scatters masses of clouds on the Vindhya mountain.
Shlok: महालतानां दामानि व्यधमत् तरसा कपिः ।  यथा प्रावृषि वेगेन मेघजालानि मारुतः ॥

Translation: The tiger among monkeys beheld a delightingful mountain, resembling the raincloud with tall, pleasing peaks, wonderful peaks spread all over the mountain. There were caves built of stone, with a variety of trees.
Shlok: ततोऽम्बुधरसङ्काशं प्रवृद्धशिखरं गिरिम्।

Translation: विचित्रकूटं कूटैश्च सर्वतः परिवारितम्।।

Shlok: ददर्श च नगात्तस्मान्नदीं निपतितां कपिः। अङ्कादिव समुत्पत्य प्रियस्य पतितां प्रियाम्।। जले निपतिताग्रैश्च पादपैरुपशोभिताम्। वार्यमाणामिव क्रुद्धां प्रमदां प्रियबन्धुभिः।।

Translation: loved one, and adorned with trees, whose boughs had bent down to the level of water, and thus looking like an enraged young woman, leaving her loved one, being detained by her near and dear ones.

Shlok: ददर्श च नगात्तस्मान्नदीं निपतितां कपिः। अङ्कादिव समुत्पत्य प्रियस्य पतितां प्रियाम्।। जले निपतिताग्रैश्च पादपैरुपशोभिताम्। वार्यमाणामिव क्रुद्धां प्रमदां प्रियबन्धुभिः।।
पुनरावृत्ततोयां च ददर्श स महाकपिः। प्रसन्नामिव कान्तस्य कान्तां पुनरुपस्थिताम्।।

Translation: He beheld several pieces of land and streams flowing out of the springs. He also noticed golden trees asresplendent as fire.

Shlok: सोऽपश्यद्भूमिभागांश्च गर्तप्रस्रवणानि च।

Translation: सुवर्णवृक्षानपरान् ददर्श शिखिसन्निभान्।।
He saw trees resplendent with golden radiance and thought that he was in the midst of gold like the Sungod getting golden hue by the radiance of Meru, the golden mountain.
Shlok: तेषां द्रुमाणां प्रभया मेरोरिव महाकपिः ।  अमन्यत तदा वीरः काञ्चनोऽस्मीति सर्वतः ॥ ३९ ॥
तां स नन्दनसङ्काशां मृगपक्षिभिरावृताम्। हर्म्यप्रासादसम्बाधां कोकिलाकुलनिस्स्वनाम्।।

Translation: There were thousands of ashoka trees some of which shone like gold, others like the flames of fire and some dark as collyrium.

Shlok: विवृद्धमूला बहवश्शोभन्ते स्म सुपुष्पिताः। शातकुम्भनिभाः केचित्केचिदग्निशिखोपमाः।।

Translation: There were thousands of ashoka trees some of which shone like gold, others like the flames of fire and some dark as collyrium.

Shlok: विवृद्धमूला बहवश्शोभन्ते स्म सुपुष्पिताः।

Translation: शातकुम्भनिभाः केचित्केचिदग्निशिखोपमाः।।
The grove with different types of gardens spread over looked like the Nandana garden of Indra and Chaitraratha garden of Kubera. It surpassed every other garden.
Shlok: नीलाञ्जननिभाः केचित् तत्राशोकाः सहस्त्रशः । नन्दनं विबुधोद्यानं चित्रं चैत्ररथं यथा ॥ ११ ॥

Translation: It was unimaginable in splendour. It was divine and delightful filled with the radiance of countless varieties of blossoms shining like stars, like a second firmament. It was like another ocean filled with precious gems of flowers.
Shlok: अतिवृत्तमिवाचिन्त्यं दिव्यं रम्यश्रियायुतम् ।  द्वितीयमिव चाकाशं पुष्पज्योतिर्गणायुतम् ॥ १२ ॥

Translation: The monkey leader saw a lofty templelike structure in the midst of the Ashoka grove which was highly fragrant and appeared like another indescribable structure that stood on a thousand pillars like another Gandhamadana mountain.
Shlok: शैलेन्द्रमिव गन्धाढ्यं द्वितीयं गन्धमादनम्। अशोकवनिकायां तु तस्यां वानरपुङ्गवः।।

Translation: It gleamed white like mount Kailasa. Its stairs were paved with corals. The altars were made of brightly polished gold.
Shlok: स ददर्शाविदूरस्थं चैत्यप्रासादमुच्छ्रितम्।

Translation: मथ्ये स्तम्भसहस्रेण स्थितं कैलासपाण्डुरम्।।

Then he beheld a lady surrounded by female demons. Clad in soiled clothes she looked dejected, emaciated through fasting and was sighing repeatedly. She appeared thin and pale like the crescent Moon at the beginning of the bright fortnight.
Shlok: उपवासकृशां दीनां निश्श्वसन्तीं पुनः पुनः।

Translation: ददर्श शुक्लपक्षादौ चन्द्ररेखामिवामलाम्।।
Her form was faintly recognisable. She had a lovely radiance on account of her beautiful form. She looked like the tip of burning fire engulfed in a cloud of smoke.
Shlok: मन्दप्रख्यायमानेन रूपेण रुचिरप्रभाम्। पिनद्धां धूमजालेन शिखामिव विभावसोः।।

Translation: She was wearing an excellent single yellow cloth which was soiled. Unadorned, she looked like a muddy lotuspond bereft of lotuses.
Shlok: पीतेनैकेन संवीतां क्लिष्टेनोत्तमवाससा। सपङ्कामनलङ्कारां विपद्मामिव पद्मिनीम्।।

Translation: She was bashful, tormented with agony, dejected with a withered look. She appeared like the star Rohini oppressed by planet Mars.
Shlok: व्रीडितां दुःखसन्तप्तां परिम्लानां तपस्विनीम्।

Translation: ग्रहेणाङ्गारकेणेव पीडितामिव रोहिणीम्।।
Unable to see her dear kith and kin, she sat guarded by ogresses. She appeared like a doe separated from the herd and encircled by a pack of hounds.
Shlok: प्रियं जनमपश्यन्तीं पश्यन्तीं राक्षसीगणम्। स्वगणेन मृगीं हीनां श्वगणाभिवृतामिव।।

Translation: She (from behind) appeared like the earth covered with a range of trees at the end of rainy season with her single long black braid touching her hips looking like a black serpent.
Shlok: नीलनागाभया वेण्या जघनं गतयैकया।

Translation: नीलया नीरदापाये वनराज्या महीमिव।।
She had a slender waist, beautiful round breasts, shapely eyebrows, red lips, dark hair, and eyes like lotus petals with attractive limbs. She was comparable to Rati, consort of Cupid.
Shlok: तां नीलकेशीं बिम्बोष्ठीं सुमध्यां सुप्रतिष्ठिताम्।

Translation: सीतां पद्मपलाशाक्षीं मन्मथस्य रतिं यथा।।
Just as the radiance of the full moon is cherished by all, this lady was liked by every one in this world. With her lovely figure she was seated on the ground like an austere ascetic.
Shlok: इष्टां सर्वस्य जगतः पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभामिव।

Translation: भूमौ सुतनुमासीनां नियतामिव तापसीम्।।
Just as the radiance of the full moon is cherished by all, this lady was liked by every one in this world. With her lovely figure she was seated on the ground like an austere ascetic.
Shlok: इष्टां सर्वस्य जगतः पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभामिव। भूमौ सुतनुमासीनां नियतामिव तापसीम्।।

Translation: The timid lady was hissing (sighing) like the consort of the serpent king, who being caught in a widespread cobweb of grief was looking gloomy.
Shlok: निःश्वासबहुलां भीरुं भुजगेन्द्रवधूमिव। शोकजालेन महता विततेन न राजतीम्।।

Translation: She was like the flames of fire obscured by smoke. She appeared like the text of Smriti of doubtful meaning, a treasure that has been thrown away
Shlok: संसक्तां धूमजालेन शिखामिव विभावसोः। तां स्मृतीमिव सन्दिग्धामृद्धिं निपतितामिव।।

Translation: Covered with dirt and mud and shorn of adornments even though she deserved them, she looked wretched like the radiance of the Moon muffled by dark clouds.

Shlok: मलपङ्कधरां दीनां मण्डनार्हाममण्डिताम्।

Translation: प्रभां नक्षत्रराजस्य कालमेघैरिवावृताम्।।
Hanuman did recognise Sita after looking at her carefully again and again even as one is able to make out knowledge of shastriclore forgotten with lapse of time and lack of practice.

Shlok: तस्य संदिदिहे बुद्धिर्मुहुः सीतां निरीक्ष्य तु।

Translation: आम्नायानामयोगेन विद्यां प्रशिथिलामिव।।

Just as an unclear expression which has undergone certain changes in meaning due to lack of usage over a long period is understood by virtue of previous practice so also Hanuman had difficulty in recognising Sita who was devoid of any decoration.

Shlok: दुःखेन बुबुधे सीतां हनुमाननलङ्कृताम्। संस्कारेण यथा हीनां वाचमर्थान्तरं गताम्।।

Translation: Just as river Ganga is not agitated by the rainbearing clouds, this Sita is not perturbed as she is aware of the prowess of Rama and might of Lakshmana
Shlok: रामस्य व्यवसायज्ञा लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः। नात्यर्थं क्षुभ्यते देवी गङ्गेव जलदागमे।।

Translation: Rama killed Viradha of fearsome valour in the forest like Sambara by Indra.

Shlok: विराधश्च हतः सङ्ख्ये राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः। वने रामेण विक्रम्य महेन्द्रेणेव शम्बरः।।

Translation: Fourteen thousand ogres of terrible deeds were made short work of in Janasthāna by means of arrows resembling tongues of fire.
Shlok: चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्।

Translation: निहतानि जनस्थाने शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः।।
Rama deserves to see her.Just as a thirsty man longs for the source of water, Rama pines for this highly virtuous lady who is tormented by Ravana
Shlok: इमां तु शीलसम्पन्नां द्रष्टुमर्हति राघवः।

Translation: रावणेन प्रमथितां प्रपामिव पिपासितः।।
Just as a king who had lost his kingdom feels happy on regaining it, surely Raghava will feel exhilarated when he gets her back.

Shlok: अस्या नूनं पुनर्लाभाद्राघवः प्रीतिमेष्यति। राजा राज्यपरिभ्रष्टः पुनः प्राप्येव मेदिनीम्।।

Translation: She who has beautiful eyes like lotus petals, was protected by the arms of both Rama and Lakshmna, who is tolerant like the earth and is guarded by the female demons of hideous appearance under a tree.
Shlok: क्षतिक्षमा पुष्करसन्निभाक्षी या रक्षिता राघवलक्ष्मणाभ्याम्। सा राक्षसीभिर्विकृतेक्षणाभिः संरक्ष्यते सम्प्रति वृक्षमूले।।

Translation: She who has beautiful eyes like lotus petals, was protected by the arms of both Rama and Lakshmna, who is tolerant like the earth and is guarded by the female demons of hideous appearance under a tree.
Shlok: क्षतिक्षमा पुष्करसन्निभाक्षी या रक्षिता राघवलक्ष्मणाभ्याम्।

Translation: सा राक्षसीभिर्विकृतेक्षणाभिः संरक्ष्यते सम्प्रति वृक्षमूले।।
Then the Moon shining like a bed of lilies rose stainless, ascended the clear sky and looked like a swan swimming through blue water.

Shlok: ततः कमुदषण्डाभो निर्मलं निर्मलोदयः। प्रजगाम नभश्चन्द्रो हंसो नीलमिवोदकम्।।

Translation: Then he saw Sita whose face shone like the fullmoon. But she was as though sinking under the burden of sorrow, like a boat with heavy load sinking in water.
Shlok: स ददर्श ततः सीतां पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्। शोकभारैरिव न्यस्तां भारैर्नावमिवाम्भसि।।

Translation: Shorn of lustre, unkempt hair filled with dust, she appeared like a meteor slipped and fallen on land, merits exhausted.

Shlok: निष्प्रभां शोकसन्तप्तां मलसङ्कुलमूर्धजाम्। क्षीणपुण्यां च्युतां भूमौ तारां निपतितामिव।।

Translation: Besieged by the demon king, deprived of her near and dear ones, Sita was looking like a fettered female elephant separated from its herd and besieged by lions.

Shlok: राक्षसाधिपसंरुद्धां बन्धुभिश्च विना कृताम्।

Translation: वियूथां सिंहसंरुद्धां बद्धां गजवधूमिव।।

She appeared like a streak (crescent) of Moon covered by autumnal clouds at the close of the rainy season. She looked haggard since she was out of contact with her husband an unused lute with its strings let loose.

Shlok: चन्द्ररेखां पयोदान्ते शारदाभ्रैरिवावृताम्।

Translation: क्लिष्टरूपामसंस्पर्शादयुक्तामिव वल्लकीम्।।

She deserves to be with Rama, but had fallen under the sway of shedemons. Sitting in the midst of Ashoka grove she was like a creeper without blossoms. Immersed in the ocean of sorrow the noble lady was like the star Rohini surrounded by unpropitious planets.

Shlok: ताभिः परिवृतां तत्र संग्रहामिव रोहिणीम्। ददर्श हनुमान् देवीं लतामकुसुमामिव।।

Translation: Even though she was daubed with dirt, and had no ornaments on her, she looked bright like a lotus fibre smeared with mud.

Shlok: सा मलेन च दिग्धाङ्गी वपुषा चाप्यलङ्कृता। मृणाली पङ्कदिग्धेव विभाति न विभाति च।।

Translation: Seeing the fawneyed Sita, a frightened female deer looking all around (as if for some help) sighing hot breath, was as though burning the trees having tender leaves with her hot sighs. She looked like a collective mass of all sorrows, a high tide of suffering.
Shlok: तां दृष्ट्वा हनुमान् सीतां मृगशावनिभेक्षणाम्। मृगकन्यामिव त्रस्तां वीक्षमाणां समन्ततः।।

Translation: Seeing the fawneyed Sita, a frightened female deer looking all around (as if for some help) sighing hot breath, was as though burning the trees having tender leaves with her hot sighs. She looked like a collective mass of all sorrows, a high tide of suffering.

Shlok: दहन्तीमिव निःश्वासैर्वृक्षान् पल्लवधारिणः। संघातमिव शोकानां दुःखस्योर्मिमिवोत्थिताम्।।

Translation: Ravana, son of sage Paulasti, was followed by a hundred women, just as Indra is trailed by the females of gods and gandharvas.

Shlok: अङ्गनाशतमात्रं तु तं व्रजन्तमनुव्रजत्।

Translation: महेन्द्रमिव पौलस्त्यं देवगन्धर्वयोषितः।।
Another shedemon moved behind him holding an umbrella with a golden handle which was white like a royal swan and bright like the fullmoon.

Shlok: राजहंसप्रतीकाशं छत्रं पूर्णशशिप्रभम्।

Translation: सौवर्णदण्डमपरा गृहीत्वा पृष्ठतो ययौ।।
Another shedemon moved behind him holding an umbrella with a golden handle which was white like a royal swan and bright like the fullmoon.

Shlok: राजहंसप्रतीकाशं छत्रं पूर्णशशिप्रभम्।

Translation: सौवर्णदण्डमपरा गृहीत्वा पृष्ठतो ययौ।।
he chief wives of Ravana with eyes dizzy with sleep and drinking followed their heroic husband like streaks of lightning follow a thunder cloud.
Shlok: निद्रामदपरीताक्ष्यो रावणस्योत्तमाः स्त्रियः। अनुजग्मुः पतिं वीरं घनं विद्युल्लता इव।।

Translation: Hanuman saw him, who was possessed of lust, arrogance and intoxication. He appeared like Cupid setting aside his quiver and arrows with his curved, big, red eyes.
Shlok: कामदर्पमदैर्युक्तं जिह्मताम्रायतेक्षणम्।

Translation: समक्षमिव कन्दर्पमपविद्धशरासनम्।।

The brilliant vanara looked at the son of Visravas (Ravana), the demon king adorned with wonderful ornaments. He had long tapering ears. He was intoxicated with drink. Encircled by damsels, he was looking like the Moon surrounded by stars.

Shlok: वृतः परमनारीभिस्ताराभिरिव चन्द्रमाः।

Translation: तं ददर्श महातेजास्तेजोवन्तं महाकपिः।।

On just seeing Ravana, the lord of demons from a distance, adorned with the best of ornaments the charming, young, blameles princess Vaidehi of beautiful waist trembled like a banana plant shaken by a strong wind.

Shlok: ततो दृष्ट्वैव वैदेही रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्।

Translation: प्रावेपत वरारोहा प्रवाते कदली यथा।।
The tennecked Ravana, too, on his part saw Sita, tormented with grief, guarded by the shedemons like a boat sunk in the sea.

Shlok: दशग्रीवस्तु वैदेहीं रक्षितां राक्षसीगणैः।

Translation: ददर्श सीतां दुःखार्तां नावं सन्नामिवार्णवे।।
She looked woeful seated on the bare earth like the broken branch of a tree cut and fallen down on the ground.

Shlok: असंवृतायामासीनां धरण्यां संशितव्रताम्।

Translation: छिन्नां प्रपतितां भूमौ शाखामिव वनस्पतेः।।
Her body looked colourful with dust. Although she deserved adornment, she had none. She was like a lotus stem in mud looking bright yet dull (with mud).
Shlok: मलमण्डनचित्राङ्गीं मण्डनार्हाममण्डिताम्।

Translation: मृणाली पङ्कदिग्धेव विभाति न विभाति च।।
Sitting in that manner she resembled a coiled serpent queen, the star Rohini overshadowed by a smoking comet (that is Ravana).

Shlok: वेष्टमानां तथाऽविष्टां पन्नगेन्द्रवधूमिव।

Translation: धूप्यमानां ग्रहेणेव रोहिणीं धूमकेतुना।।
She resembled reputation besmirched by scandals, like Vedic studies slackened by lack of aplication.
Shlok: अभूतेनापवादेन कीर्तिं निपतितामिव। आम्नायानामयोगेन विद्यां प्रशिथिलामिव।।
सन्नामिव महाकीर्तिं श्रद्धामिव विमानिताम्।

Translation: पूजामिव परिक्षीणामाशां प्रतिहतामिव।।5.19.12।।
She was like a prospect blasted, command flouted, entire direction set on flames at the time of catastrophe and articles of worship abducted by evil forces at the sacrificial ceremony.
Shlok: आयतीमिव विध्वस्तामाज्ञां प्रतिहतामिव। दीप्तामिव दिशं काले पूजामपहृतामिव।।

Translation: She was like a lotuscreeper blighted, an army with its gallant warriors killed, radiance of light blocked by darkness and a stream run dry.

Shlok: पद्मिनीमिव विध्वस्तां हतशूरां चमूमिव। प्रभामिव तमोध्वस्तामुपक्षीणामिवापगाम्।।

Translation: (She was) like the altar of worship defiled, blazing fire extinguished, and the Moon eclipsed by Rahu in the full moon night.
Shlok: वेदीमिव परामृष्टां शान्तामग्निशिखामिव। पौर्णमासीमिव निशां राहुग्रस्तेन्दुमण्डलाम्।।

Translation: (She appeared) like a lotuspond the excellent leaves of whose lotuses surrounded by frightened birds are destroyed by the trunks of elephants.
Shlok: उत्कृष्टपर्णकमलां वित्रासितविहङ्गमाम्। हस्तिहस्तपरामृष्टामाकुलां पद्मिनीमिव।।

Translation: Stricken with grief caused by separation from her husband, she appeared like a river gone thin and dry, not fit for ablution, like a night during dark fortnight of the month deprived of all its glow.

Shlok: पतिशोकातुरां शुष्कां नदीं विस्रावितामिव। परया मृजया हीनां कृष्णपक्षनिशामिव।।

Translation: A delicate lady with beautiful limbs who deserved to be in a gemcrusted house was (now) like a lotus stem just plucked out and scorched by the Sun's heat.
Shlok: सुकुमारीं सुजाताङ्गीं रत्नगर्भगृहोचिताम्। तप्यमानामिवोष्णेन मृणालीमचिरोद्धृताम्।।

Translation: She was sighing heavily in intense grief like a royal female elephant tied to a pillar and separated from her lord, the leader of the herd.
Shlok: गृहीतामालितां स्तम्भे यूथपेन विनाकृताम्। निःश्वसन्तीं सुदुःखार्तां गजराजवधूमिव।।

Translation: She was lovely even with a single braid of unkempt hair like the earth with a single row of dark trees covering its surface at the end of the rainy season.
Shlok: एकया दीर्घया वेण्या शोभमानामयत्नतः। नीलया नीरदापाये वनराज्या महीमिव।।

Translation: Your charming youth should not pass away (uselessly). A past event does not come back like a current of stream.
Shlok: इदं ते चारु सञ्जातं यौवनं व्यतिवर्तते। यदतीतं पुनर्नैति स्रोतः शीघ्रमपामिव।।

Translation: O lady with auspicious looks Me thinks, the creator must have retired after creating your beautiful form. For there is no one comparable to you in beauty.
Shlok: त्वां कृत्वोपरतो मन्ये रूपकर्ता स विश्वसृक्।

Translation: न हि रूपोपमा त्वन्या तवास्ति शुभदर्शने।।
O one with a face like the cool fullmoon, with heavy hips. I am unable to extricate my eyes from any limb (of your body) I see.
Shlok: यद्यत्पश्यामि ते गात्रं शीतांशुसदृशानने।

Translation: तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् पृथुश्रोणि चक्षुर्मम निबध्यते।।
O Vaidehi I wonder if Rama can see you at all. You are like moonlight veiled by dark clouds and cannot be seen even by the flying cranes.
Shlok: न हि वैदेहि रामस्त्वां द्रष्टुं वा प्युपलप्स्यते।

Translation: पुरोबलाकैरसितैर्मेघैर्ज्योत्स्नामिवावृताम्।।
O lovely, timid lady your smile, your teeth and your eyes are bewitching. Just as Garuda snatches away a serpent, you ravish my mind by your beauty.

Shlok: चारुस्मिते चारुदति चारुनेत्रे विलासिनि।

Translation: मनो हरसि मे भीरु सुपर्णः पन्नगं यथा।।

Shlok: मम ह्यसितकेशान्ते त्रैलोक्यप्रवराः स्त्रियः।

Translation: तास्त्वां परिचरिष्यन्ति श्रियमप्सरसो यथा।।
O queen Rama is not equal to me either in penance or prowess or valour or wealth or brilliance or even in fame.
Shlok: न रामस्तपसा देवि न बलेन न विक्रमैः।

Translation: न धनेन मया तुल्यस्तेजसा यशसापि वा।।
Turn your mind away from me and fix it on your wives. You should not expect to seek me just as a sinner cannot hope to seek blessedness.

Shlok: निवर्तय मनो मत्तः स्वजने क्रियतां मनः। न मां प्रार्थयितुं युक्तं सुसिद्धिमिव पापकृत्।।

Translation: O nightranger Enjoy your wives. Take care of them. Taking your example, others' wives also deserve to be protected.
Shlok: यथा तव तथान्येषां दारा रक्ष्या निशाचर। आत्मानमुपमां कृत्वा स्वेषु दारेषु रम्यताम्।।

Translation: I cannot be lured by your power or wealth. I am inseparable from Raghava like light from the Sun.

Shlok: शक्या लोभयितुं नाहमैश्वर्येण धनेन वा। अनन्या राघवेणाहं भास्करेण प्रभा यथा।।

Translation: I am alone the lawful wife of the lord of the earth like the knowledge of the Vedas which rightfully belongs to a wise brahmin who has realised the self after having had his ceremonial bath (as a token of celibacy) and having observed strict vows during the period of his study.

Shlok: अहमौपयिकी भार्या तस्यैव वसुधापतेः। व्रतस्नातस्य विप्रस्य विद्येव विदितात्मनः।।

Translation: O Ravana it is proper for you to unite me in distress with Rama as one would unite a female elephant with the lordly elephant from which it is separated in the wilderness.
Shlok: साधु रावण रामेण मां समानय दुःखिताम्। वने वाशितया सार्धं करेण्वेव गजाधिपम्।।

Translation: You will hear the terrible twang of Rama's bow resembling the rumble of the thunderbolt released by Indra who performed a hundred yajnas.
Shlok: रामस्य धनुषः शब्दं श्रोष्यसि त्वं महास्वनम्। शतक्रतुविसृष्टस्य निर्घोषमशनेरिव।।

Translation: Arrows marked with Rama and Lakshmana will soon rain on Lanka like the poisonous snakes with flaming fangs.
Shlok: इह शीघ्रं सुपर्वाणो ज्वलितास्या इवोरगा: । इषवो निपतिष्यन्ति रामलक्ष्मणलक्षणाः।।

Translation: Just as Garuda swiftly extirpates the serpents, Rama will exterminate the demon leaders.

Shlok: राक्षसेन्द्रमहासर्पान् स रामगरुडो महान्। उद्धरिष्यति वेगेन वैनतेय इवोरगान्।।

Translation: Had you smelt the presence of Rama and Lakshmna, it would not have been possible for you to stand there, like a dog under the gaze of a pair of tigers.
Shlok: न हि गन्धमुपाघ्राय रामलक्ष्मणयोस्त्वया। शक्यं संदर्शने स्थातुं शुना शार्दूलयोरिव।।

Translation: My lord Rama accompanied by Saumitri will draw out your life by his arrows swiftly as Aditya sucks up shallow water at once by his radiance.
Shlok: क्षिप्रं तव स नाथो मे रामः सौमित्रिणा सह। तोयमल्पमिवादित्यः प्राणानादास्यते शरैः।।

Translation: Even if you fly to Kubera's mountain (Kailasa) or the residence of king Varuna (ocean) you will not escape Rama's arrows like a mighty tree cannot evade lightning.
Shlok: गिरिं कुबेरस्य गतोऽथ वालयं सभां गतो वा वरुणस्य राज्ञः। असंशयं दाशरथेर्न मोक्ष्यसे महाद्रुमः कालहतोऽशनेरिव।।

Translation: My love for you has restrained my anger, just as a good charioteer controls the horses galloping on a wrong path.

Shlok: सन्नियच्छति मे क्रोधं त्वयि कामः समुत्थितः।

Translation: द्रवतोऽमार्गमासाद्य हयानिव सुसारथिः।।
Who in all the three worlds other than you would, even in mind, seek this consort of the righteous self (Sri Rama) like Sachi to Indra? .

Shlok: मां हि धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं शचीमिव शचीपतेः।

Translation: त्वदन्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रार्थयेन्मनसापि कः।।
It is like a proud elephant fighting in war with a rabbit. Rama is like an elephant and you are like an ordinary rabbit people speak of.

Shlok: यथा दृप्तश्च मातङ्गः शशश्च सद्दृशो युधि।

Translation: तथा मातङ्गवद्रामस्त्वं नीच: शशवत् स्मृतः।।
Prosperous Ravana looked like a mass of dark cloud, with strong arms, stout neck, gait of a lion, a blazing tongue and burning eyes

Shlok: नीलजीमूतसङ्काशो महाभुजशिरोधरः। सिंहसत्त्वगतिः श्रीमान् दीप्त जिह्वाग्रलोचनः।।

Translation: Wrapped well with a big black thread around his hips, he appeared like mount Mandara encompassed by a black serpent at the time of churning the milkocean for nectar.
Shlok: श्रोणिसूत्रेण महता मेचकेन सुसंवृतः।

Translation: अमृतोत्पादनद्धेन भुजगेनेव मन्दरः।।
The lord of demons shone like mount Mandara, both his long two arms like two mountain peaks.

Shlok: ताभ्यां स परिपूर्णाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां राक्षसेश्वरः।

Translation: शुशुभेऽचलसङ्काशः शृङ्गाभ्यामिव मन्दरः।।
He stood like a mountain with two Ashoka trees clothed with red leaves and flowers in the form of earrings of the colour of the rising Sun.

Shlok: तरुणादित्यवर्णाभ्यां कुण्डलाभ्यां विभूषितः।

Translation: रक्तपल्लवपुष्पाभ्यामशोकाभ्यामिवाचलः।।
He was comparable to the wishfulfilling tree grown in heaven, a personified spring season and a memorial structure raised on the cremation ground. He looked frightening even though welladorned.
Shlok: स कल्पवृक्षप्रतिमो वसन्त इव मूर्तिमान्।

Translation: श्मशानचैत्यप्रतिमो भूषितोऽपि भयङ्करः।।
Looking at Vaidehi, eyes red with anger, and breathing heavily like a histing snake, Ravana replied:

Shlok: अवेक्षमाणो वैदेहीं कोपसंरक्तलोचनः।

Translation: उवाच रावणः सीतां भुजङ्ग इव निःश्वसन्।।
O Sita you are following a vow of chastity and treading a meaningless, wrong path. I will destroy you as the Sun dispels the morning twilight with his lustre
Shlok: अनयेनाभिसम्पन्नमर्थहीनमनुव्रते।

Translation: नाशयाम्यहमद्य त्वां सूर्यः सन्ध्यामिवौजसा।।
Having heard her words, the demon king who resembled a fierce dark cloud turned away, laughing heartily.

Shlok: एवमुक्तस्तु राक्षस्या समुत्क्षिप्तस्ततो बली।

Translation: प्रहसन्मेघसङ्काशो राक्षसः स न्यवर्तत।।
Thereupon the tennecked demon departed, as if he was shaking the earth and entered his residence which was shining like the blazing midday Sun.
Shlok: प्रस्थितः स दशग्रीवः कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्।

Translation: ज्वलद्भास्करवर्णाभं प्रविवेश निवेशनम्।।
Accept as your husband the demon king Ravana, courageous and handsome like Indra, king of the gods generous, sacrificing and pleasing.

Shlok: रावणं भज भर्तारं भर्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम्।

Translation: विक्रान्तं रूपवन्तं च सुरेशमिव वासवम्।।
O beautiful Sita Just like Swaha, queen to the Firegod and Sachi to Indra, accept Ravana. Why are you still thinking of Rama who is helpless and whose life span is coming to an end soon.
Shlok: अग्नेः स्वाहा यथा देवी शची वेन्द्रस्य शोभने।

Translation: किं ते रामेण वैदेहि कृपणेन गतायुषा।।
I have developed a morbid desire to feast upon this woman with eyes flashing like doe's, whose breasts heave with stress and fear after she was abducted by Ravana.
Shlok: इमां हरिणलोलाक्षीं त्रासोत्कम्पिपयोधराम्।

Translation: रावणेन हृतां दृष्टवा दौहृदो मे महानभूत्।।
Threatened by the ogresses in that manner, Sita who was like the daughter of a god, cried aloud.
Shlok: एवं संभर्त्स्यमाना सा सीता सुरसुतोपमा।

Translation: राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर्दैर्यमुत्सृज्य रोदिति।।
Surrounded by the ogresses, distressed Sita, who was like the daughter of a divine, did not get any solace.

Shlok: सा राक्षसीमध्यगता सीता सुरसुतोपमा। न शर्म लेभे दुःखार्ता रावणेन च तर्जिता।।

Translation: Like a doe that strayed from the herd in the forest and tormented by wolves around, Sita had withdrawn into herself all her limbs through fear, she was trembling excessively.
Shlok: वेपते स्माधिकं सीता विशन्ती वाङ्गमात्मनः।

Translation: वने यूथपरिभ्रष्टा मृगी कोकैरिवार्दिता।।
Trembling like a banana tree uprooted by the stormy wind, Sita who was seized with fear of the ogresses looked pale and desperate.

Shlok: सा वेपमाना पतिता प्रवाते कदली यथा।

Translation: राक्षसीनां भयत्रस्ता विवर्णवदनाभवत्।।
The long, luxuriant braid of hair of the trembling Sita waving (in the wind), appeared like a crawling female serpent.

Shlok: तस्याः सा दीर्घविपुला वेपन्त्या सीतया तदा।

Translation: ददृशे कम्पिनी वेणी व्यालीव परिसर्पती।।
I am a woman of low merit, a wretched woman, an orphan. I will be ruined like the loaded boat that gets hit in the midst of the ocean by the stormy wind.
Shlok: एषाल्पपुण्या कृपणा विनशिष्याम्यनाथवत्।

Translation: समुद्रमध्ये नौः पूर्णा वायुवेगैरिवाहता।।
Unable to find my husband and seized by these ogresses, I am collapsing on account of grief like a riverbank under the current of water.

Shlok: भर्तारं तमपश्यन्ती राक्षसीवशमागता। सीदामि खलु शोकेन कूलं तोयहतं यथा।।

Translation: Blessed are those who are in touch with my husband with eyes like lotus petals, whose walk is majestic like a lion's, who has a sense of gratitude and is pleasing in words.
Shlok: तं पद्मदलपत्राक्षं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्।

Translation: धन्याः पश्यन्ति मे नाथं कृतज्ञं प्रियवादिनम्।।
Separated from Rama endowed with selfknowledge, it is impossible for me to live like one who has drunk venom.

Shlok: सर्वथा तेन हीनाया रामेण विदितात्मना।

Translation: तीक्ष्णं विषमिवास्वाद्य दुर्लभं मम जीवितम्।।
Bewildered or distracted or intoxicated, this young lady wailed, wallowing round on the ground like a young female horse:

Shlok: उन्मत्तेव प्रमत्तेव भ्रान्तचित्तेव शोचती।

Translation: उपावृत्ता किशोरीव विवेष्टन्ती महीतले।।
Like me weeping, the cry of ogresses with lost husbands will be heard in every house in Lanka. There is no doubt.

Shlok: ततो निहतनाथानां राक्षसीनां गृहे गृहे।

Translation: यथाहमेवं रुदती तथा भूयो न संशयः।।
Very soon this Lanka will be enveloped with smoke from funeral pyres and thronged with flocks of vultures moving in circles. It will be like a burial ground.
Shlok: चिताधूमाकुलपथा गृध्रमण्डलसङ्कुला।

Translation: अचिरेण तु लङ्केयं श्मशानसदृशी भवेत्।।
Surely this impregnable Lanka will wither up (lose its splendour) and appear like a widow when this sinful Ravana, a mean demon is killed.

Shlok: नूनं लङ्का हते पापे रावणे राक्षसाधमे।

Translation: शोषं यास्यति दुर्धर्षा प्रमदा विधवा यथा।।

Shlok: पुण्योत्सवसमुत्था च नष्टभर्त्री सराक्षसी। भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का नष्टभर्त्री यथाङ्गना।।
धन्या देवास्सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। मम पश्यन्ति ये नाथं रामं राजीवलोचनम्।।
किं नु मे न गुणाः केचित्किं वा भाग्यक्षयो मम।

Translation: याहं सीदामि रामेण हीना मुख्येन भामिनी।।
Just as light is united with the Sun, I saw Sita united with Rama. I saw Rama with Lakshmana riding a huge, mountainlike elephant having four tusks.

Shlok: रामेण सङ्गता सीता भास्करेण प्रभा यथा।

Translation: राघवश्च मया दृष्टश्चतुर्दष्ट्रं महागजम्।।
Dressed in white garlands and clothes, the two brothers, tigers among men, glowing in their effulgence approached Janaki.
Shlok: आरूढ श्शैलसङ्काशं चचार सहलक्ष्मणः। ततस्तौ नरशार्दूलौ दीप्यमानौ स्वतेजसा।।

Translation: Valiant Rama, foremost among men, accompanied by his brother Lakshmana and wife Sita went towards the northerly direction in the wonderful Pushpaka chariot that resembled the Sun.

Shlok: लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया सह वीर्यवान्।

Translation: आरुह्य पुष्पकं दिव्यं विमानं सूर्यसन्निभम्।।
Just as a sinner cannot attain heaven Rama cannot be won by gods or demons, even rakshasas and others
Shlok: न हि रामो महातेजाश्शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः।

Translation: राक्षसैर्वापि चान्यैर्वा स्वर्गः पापजनैरिव।।

Shlok: सहसोत्थाय संभ्रान्तो भयार्तो मदविह्वलः।

Translation: उन्मत्त इव दिग्वासा दुर्वाक्यं प्रलपन्बहु।।

Shlok: शङ्खदुन्धुभिनिर्घोषैर्नृत्तगीतैरलङ्कृतः।

Translation: आरुह्य शैलसङ्काशं मेघस्तनितनिस्स्वनम्।।
This dream indeed served as an augery for good news about her. Look, her (left) eye which is large like a lotus petal is throbbing.

Shlok: निमित्तभूतमेतत्तु श्रोतुमस्या महत्प्रियम्।

Translation: दृश्यते च स्फुरच्चक्षुः पद्मपत्रमिवायतम्।।
Her excellent left thigh, comparable to a female elephant's trunk is trembling, as though indicating that Rama is standing in her presence.

Shlok: करेणुहस्तप्रतिम स्सव्यश्चोरुरनुत्तमः।

Translation: वेपमानः सूचयति राघवं पुरतः स्थितम्।।

After hearing the unpleasant words spoken by the king of demons, which caused restlessness and sorrow to Sita, she was terrified like the young calf of a lordly elephant fallen into the clutches of a lion in the midst of the forest.

Shlok: सा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वचो निशम्य तद्रावणस्याप्रियमप्रियार्ता।

Translation: सीता वितत्रास यथा वनान्ते सिंहाभिपन्ना गजराजकन्या।।
Encircled by the demonesses, Sita was repeatedly humiliated by Ravana's cruel words.She wept like a young girl deserted in a desolate forest.

Shlok: सा राक्षसीमध्यगता च भीरु र्वाग्भिर्भृशं रावणतर्जिता च।

Translation: कान्तारमध्ये विजने विसृष्टा बालेव कन्या विललाप सीता।।
Even though I am devoid of joy, and living in deep agony, my heart bursts not into a thousand pieces like the summit of a mountain hit by thunderbolt (lightning).

Shlok: सुखाद्विहीनं बहुदुःखपूर्ण मिदं तु नूनं हृदयं स्थिरं मे।

Translation: विशीर्यते यन्न सहस्रधाऽद्य वज्राहतं शृङ्गमिवाचलस्य।।

I will not be blamed if I commit suicide now.I stand condemned to death in the hands of this ugly Ravana. I cannot bestow my affection on him or surender to his desire like a brahmin would not like to impart Vedic knowledge to a nonbrahmin.
Shlok: नैवास्ति दोषो मम नूनमत्र वध्याहमस्याप्रियदर्शनस्य।

Translation: भावं न चास्याहमनुप्रदातु मलं द्विजो मन्त्रमिवाद्विजाय।।

If the lord of the world does not come here before that (time fixed by Ravana) the vile lord of demons will cut me into pieces with weapons just as a barber would cut to pieces the foetus with a sharp knife (in order to save a pregnant woman).

Shlok: नूनं ममाङ्गान्यचिरादनार्यः शस्त्रैश्शितैश्छेत्स्यति राक्षसेन्द्रः।

Translation: तस्मिननागच्छति लोकनाथे गर्भस्थजन्तोरिव शल्यकृन्तः।।
Alas, two months is too long a time to wait in grief. I am like a thief captured for offending a king and waiting overnight for execution at day-break
Shlok: दुःखं बतेदं मम दुःखिताया

Translation: मासौ चिरायाधिगमिष्यतो द्वौ।
बद्धस्य वध्यस्य तथा निशान्ते
राजापराधादिव तस्करस्य।।5.28.7।।

Alas! Rama, Alas! Lakshmana, Alas! Sumitra, Alas! my mother, Alas! Rama's mother, I am an ill-starred woman going to perish in this way like a light boat capsized in the midst of an ocean when the whirl-wind blows.

Shlok: हा राम हा लक्ष्मण हा सुमित्रे

Translation: हा राममातः सह मे जनन्या।
एषा विपद्याम्यहमल्पभाग्या
महार्णवे नौरिव मूढवाता।।5.28.8।।
Just like two mighty lions are killed by a bolt of lightning, the two princes must have been killed by a creature in the guise of a deer on my account.
Shlok: तरस्विनौ धारयता मृगस्य

Translation: सत्त्वेन रूपं मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रौ।
नूनं विशस्तौ मम कारणात्तौ
सिंहर्षभौ द्वाविव वैद्युतेन।।5.28.9।।

Shlok: अनन्य दैवत्वमियं क्षमा च

Translation: भूमौ च शय्या नियमश्च धर्मे।
पतिव्रतात्वं विफलं ममेदं

Her left eye with a row of curved eyelashes, the black pupils of the eye in white throbbed in an auspicious manner. The lady with her long tresses, and throbbing eye appeared like a red lotus gently struck by a fish.

Shlok: तस्याः शुभं वाममरालपक्ष्म राजीवृतं कृष्णविशालशुक्लम्।

Translation: प्रास्पन्दतैकं नयनं सुकेश्या मीनाहतं पद्ममिवाभिताम्रम्।।5.29.2।।

Reassured by such omens which augured well as tested by time, Sita, with beautiful eyebrows, and deep foresight experienced great joy, like a seed blighted by the wind and the Sun comes back to joyful life through a pleasing shower.
Shlok: एतैर्निमित्तैरपरैश्च सुभ्रूः

Translation: सम्बोधिता प्रागपि साधु सिद्धैः।
वातातपक्लान्तमिव प्रणष्टं
वर्षेण बीजं प्रतिसंजहर्ष।।5.29.6।।
Her face shining with beautiful red lips like bimba fruit, sparkling teeth, and curved eyelashes with lovely brows extending up to her hair, she appeared like a Moon released from the mouth of Rahu.

Shlok: तस्याः पुनर्बिम्बफलाधरोष्ठं

Translation: स्वक्षिभ्रुकेशान्तमरालपक्ष्म।
वक्त्रं बभासे सितशुक्लदंष्ट्रं
राहोर्मुखाच्चन्द्र इव प्रमुक्तः।।5.29.7।।

Revered Sita, completely relieved of grief, exhaustion gone, fears allayed, mind illumined with joy, looked charming with her countenance as a night with the Moon fully risen during the bright fortnight.
Shlok: सा वीतशोका व्यपनीततन्द्री

Translation: शान्तज्वरा हर्षविबुद्धसत्त्वा।
अशोभतार्या वदनेन शुक्ले
The sight of Sita who seemed a deity in the Nandana garden of Indra, set a chain of reflections in his mind :

Shlok: अवेक्षमाणस्तां देवीं देवतामिव नन्दने।

Translation: ततो बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयामास वानरः।।5.30.2।।
The moonfaced Sita had never experienced sorrow before. She sees no end to her sorrow and suffering. I will console her.

Shlok: अहमाश्वासयाम्येनां पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्।

Translation: अदृष्टदुःखां दुःखार्तां दुःखस्यान्तमगच्छतीम्।।5.30.7।।
I should provide some comfort to the strongarmed Rama with a face like the fullmoon yearning to see Sita.

Shlok: मया च स महाबाहुः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननः।

Translation: समाश्यासयितुं न्याय्यस्सीतादर्शनलालसः।।5.30.10।।
If I speak like a brahmin in sanskrit language she would be frightened thinking that I am Ravana and how would a vanara speak?

Shlok: यदि वाचं प्रदास्यामि द्विजातिरिव संस्कृताम्।

Translation: रावणं मन्यमाना मां सीता भीता भविष्यति।।5.30.18।।
If Sita screams, the horde of terrific ogresses will at once gather, armed with dreadful weapons like Yama, the god of death.

Shlok: सीतया च कृते शब्दे सहसा राक्षसीगणा:।

Translation: नानाप्रहरणो घोर: समेयादन्तकोपम:।।5.30.22।।
Even well planned diplomatic missions fail like darkness dispelled at Sunrise if the messenger is confused and if the place and time are not propitious for them.
Shlok: भूताश्चार्था विनश्यन्ति देशकालविरोधिताः।।5.30.37।।

Translation: विक्लबं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा।
He was the most virtuous among royal sages, equal to sages in austerity, born in the race of emperors and equal to Indra in might.

Shlok: राजर्षीणां गुणश्रेष्ठस्तपसा चर्षिभि स्समः।

Translation: चक्रवर्तिकुले जातः पुरन्दरसमो बले।।
His beloved eldest son Rama, whose countenance is like the full moon, is a scholar of all branches of knowledge and is foremost among the bowmen on earth.
Shlok: तस्य पुत्रः प्रियो ज्येष्ठस्ताराधिपनिभाननः।

Translation: रामो नाम विशेषज्ञः श्रेष्ठ स्सर्वधनुष्मताम्।।
Surely I have seen here a lady of similar body, of similar complexion, of similar glow and beauty as described by Rama".
Shlok: यथारूपां यथावर्णां यथालक्ष्मीवतीं च निश्चिताम्।।5.31.15।।

Translation: अश्रौषं राघवस्याहं सेयमासादिता मया।
She looked obliquely, up, and down and saw Hanuman of unimaginable intelligence, the minister of the monkey lord, son of the Windgod, who looked like the rising Sun.
Shlok: सा तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च तथाप्यधस्तान्निरीक्षमाणा तमचिन्त्यबुद्धिम्।

Translation: ददर्श पिङ्गाधिपतेरमात्यं वातात्मजं सूर्यमिवोदयस्थम्।।
Sita got perplexed on seeing him (Hanuman), who was tawny in complexion and looked like a cluster of lightnings, clad in white and hidden in between the branches.

Shlok: ततश्शाखान्तरे लीनं दृष्ट्वा चलितमानसा।  वेष्टितार्जुनवस्त्रं तं विद्युत्सङ्घातपिङ्गलम्।।

Translation: There (on the tree) she noticed a monkey like a cluster of fully blossomed Ashoka flower, shining bright, whose eyes were glowing like pure molten gold, speaking softly and pleasingly.
Shlok: सा ददर्श कपिं तत्र प्रश्रितं प्रियवादिनम्।

Translation: फुल्लाशोकोत्कराभासं तप्तचामीकरेक्षणम्।।
But no, it was not a dream for tormented by grief and sorrow I cannot have a dream. When separated from the moonfaced Rama I have no sleep or pleasure, how can I have dream?

Shlok: स्वप्नोऽपि नायं नहि मेऽस्ति निद्रा शोकेन दुःखेन च पीडितायाः।  सुखं हि मे नास्ति यतोऽस्मि हीना तेनेन्दुपूर्णप्रतिमाननेन।।

Translation: Hanuman, son of the Windgod whose face shone like coral, dressed in a sober manner climbed down the tree, went close to Sita, offered salutations with his palms on his head and spoke in sweet words
Shlok: सोऽवतीर्य द्रुमात्तस्माद्विद्रुमप्रतिमाननः।

Translation: विनीतवेषः कृपणः प्रणिपत्योपसृत्य च।।5.33.1।
O blameless lady with eyes like lotus petals, in crumpled silk, holding a branch, and standing, who are you?
Shlok: का नु पद्मपलाशाक्षि क्लिष्टकौशेयवासिनि।

Translation: द्रुमस्य शाखामालम्ब्य तिष्ठसि त्वमनिन्दिते।।
Why are tears of grief flowing from your eyes like water trickling down a pair of petals of white lotuses?
Shlok: किमर्थम् तव नेत्राभ्यां वारि स्रवति शोकजम्।

Translation: पुण्डरीकपलाशाभ्यां विप्रकीर्णमिवोदकम्।।
Rama is glorious as the Sun, brings delight to the whole world like the Moon, is the
king of kings like Vaisravana, and renowned like Visnu endowed with valour.

Shlok: आदित्य इव तेजस्वी लोककान्तश्शशी यथा।।5.34.28।।

Translation: राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवो वैश्रवणो यथा।
He is truthful in speech like Brihaspati, prosperous (like Kubera), sweettongued, handsome, graceful like Kamadeva.
Shlok: विक्रमेणोपपन्नश्च यथा विष्णुर्महायशाः। सत्यवादी मधुरवाग्देवो वाचस्पतिर्यथा।।

Translation: He is rich in comeliness, graceful and full of splendour as Love-incarnate. He punishes only him who deserves anger and is the foremost chariot-warrior in the world.
Shlok: रूपवान्सुभग श्रीमान् कन्दर्प इव मूर्तिमान्। स्थानक्रोधः प्रहर्ता च श्रेष्ठो लोके महारथः।।

Translation: Heroic Rama will soon release many scorching, fiery arrows in anger and kill Ravana. I seek your permission as an envoy of Rama. Filled with grief by your separation, he has made inquiries about your welfare.
Shlok: रोषप्रमुक्तैरिषुभिर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः।।5.34.33।।

Translation: तेनाहं प्रेषितो दूत स्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः।
O Vaidehi with eyes like lotus petals although you know your husband's and Lakshmana's form and distinguishing marks, it is my good fortune that you asked me (to describe them).
Shlok: जानन्ती बत दिष्ट्या मां वैदेहि परिपृच्छसि।

Translation: भर्तुः कमलपत्त्राक्षि संस्थानं लक्ष्मणस्य च।।
Shlok: 35.6 (lupta)

Translation: O daughter of Janaka Rama with eyes like lotus petals is a person born with a delightful form, richly endowed with indescribable charm and politeness.

Shlok: रामः कमलपत्त्राक्ष स्सर्वसत्त्वमनोहरः।

Translation: रूपदाक्षिण्यसम्पन्नः प्रसूतो जनकात्मजे।।
He vies with the Sun in effulgence, with earth in forbearance, with Brihaspati in intelligence, and in fame with Indra.
Shlok: तेजसादित्यसङ्काशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः।  बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या यशसा वासवोपमः।।

Translation: His tone is resonant like drums, he has a beautiful, dark, shining complexion. He has symmetrical, well proportioned limbs. He is neither too tall nor too short.

Shlok: दुन्दुभिस्वननिर्घोष स्स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान्।  समस्समविभक्ताङ्गो वर्णं श्यामं समाश्रितः।।

Translation: He is a person with his pairs of eyebrows, nostrils, eyes, ears, lips, nipples, elbows, wrists, knees, testicles, loins, arms, legs and buttocks in good symmetry he has four sharp teeth. He walks in different gaits like a lion, leopard, elephant and bull as occasion demands he has sharp nose, charming lips and jaws. He has smooth hair, eyes, skin, teeth and feet and his eight parts of his body namely back, trunk, limbs, fingers, toes, eyes and testicles are long.

Shlok: चतुर्दशसमद्वन्द्वश्चतुर्दंष्ट्रश्चतुर्गतिः।

Translation: महोष्ठहनुनासश्च पञ्चस्निग्धोऽष्टवंशवान्।।

Shlok: दशपद्मो दशबृहत्त्रिभिर्व्याप्तो द्विशुक्लवान्।

Translation: षडुन्नतो नवतनुस्त्रिभिर्व्याप्नोति राघवः।।
Having heard the words of Lakshmana, the king of vanaras became extremely lustreless like the Sun overshadowed by the planet Rahu.

Shlok: स श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रस्तु लक्ष्मणेनेरितं वचः।

Translation: तदासीन्निष्प्रभोऽत्यर्थं ग्रहग्रस्त इवांशुमान्।।
Rama looked at them and wept clasping them again and again in grief which inflamed like fire.
Shlok: पश्यतस्तानि रुदतस्ताम्यतश्च पुनः पुनः।

Translation: प्रादीपयन्दाशरथेस्तानि शोकहुताशनम्।।
Rama is burning like a furnace by (three fires) sleeplessness, grief and intense anxiety just as the three sacred fires keep a firesanctuary intensely heated.

Shlok: त्वत्कृते तमनिद्रा च शोकश्चिन्ता च राघवम्।

Translation: तापयन्ति महात्मानमग्न्यगारमिवाग्नयः।।
On account of sorrow caused by not being able to see you, Rama of Raghu dynasty is shaken up like a lofty mountain is shaken by earthquake.
