Shlok: तवादर्शनशोकेन राघवः प्रविचाल्यते।

Translation: महता भूमिकम्पेन महानिव शिलोच्चयः।।
Her face with large eyes with a tinge of red corners shone like the Moon released from Rahu.

Shlok: चारु तद्वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम्।

Translation: अशोभत विशालाक्ष्या राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट्।।
O noble lady I am a vanara, an envoy of learned Rama. You see this ring with Rama's name inscribed on it, O godlike lady

Shlok: वानरोऽहं महाभागे दूतो रामस्य धीमतः।

Translation: रामनामाङ्कितं चेदं पश्य देव्यङ्गुलीयकम्।।
She received the ornament that adorned her husband's hand and gazed at it and felt delighted as though her husband had arrived.

Shlok: गृहीत्वा प्रेक्षमाणा सा भर्तुः करविभूषणम्।

Translation: भर्तारमिव सम्प्राप्ता जानकी मुदिताऽभवत्।।
Her beautiful countenance with large white eyes with a reddish tinge in the corners shone like the Moon released from Rahu.

Shlok: चारु तद्वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम्।

Translation: अशोभत विशालाक्ष्या राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट्।।
The formidable Rama will not send any one specially to me without testing him or knowing his valour.
Shlok: प्रेषयिष्यति दुर्धर्षो रामो न ह्यपरीक्षितम्।

Translation: पराक्रममविज्ञाय मत्सकाशं विशेषतः।।
Hope, Rama's moonlike face without me with its golden complexion and lotus fragrance must not have been pale and withered with tears like the lotus in a pond scorched by the heat.
Shlok: कच्चिन्न तद्धेमसमानवर्णं तस्याननं पद्मसमानगन्धि।

Translation: मया विना शुष्यति शोकदीनं जलक्षये पद्ममिवातपेन।।
O lotuseyed one Rama knows not that you are here. Therefore he has not taken you away immediately as did Indra to rescue his wife Sachi.

Shlok: न त्वामिहस्थां जानीते रामः कमललोचने।

Translation: तेन त्वां नानयत्याशु शचीमिव पुरन्दरः।।
O noble lady not being able to see you, Rama is immersed in an ocean of sorrow, he has no solace like an elephant tormented by a lion.

Shlok: तवादर्शनजेनार्ये शोकेन स परिप्लुतः।

Translation: न शर्म लभते रामस्सिंहार्दित इव द्विपः।।

O Sita I swear in the name of mountains like Malaya, Vindhya, Meru, and Dardura (the abodes of monkeys and bears) and by the roots and fruits as well (which are the food of vanaras). you will soon behold Rama with beautiful eyes, red lips like bimba fruit, lovely earrings and a countenance resembling the full moon.
Shlok: यथा सुनयनं वल्गु बिम्बोष्ठं चारु कुण्डलम् ।

Translation: मुखं द्रक्ष्यसि रामस्य पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्।।
To the righteous words (about Rama's grief) of Hanuman, Sita with a face like the full moon replied.
Shlok: सीता तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानना।

Translation: हनूमन्तमुवाचेदं धर्मार्थसहितं वचः।।
When will Raghava reach the shore of this ocean of grief? He is like a man who has suffered a ship wreck, trying to swim?

Shlok: शोकस्यास्य कदा पारं राघवोऽधिगमिष्यति।

Translation: प्लवमानः परिश्रान्तो हतनौ स्सागरे यथा।।
O monkey the valiant Rama is like the Sungod shoofing a dazzling volley of arrows which will dry up the sea of enemy forces.
Shlok: शरजालांशुमान्शूरः कपे रामदिवाकरः।

Translation: शत्रुरक्षोमयं तोयमुपशोषं नयिष्यति।।
O Vaidehi you will see Rama and Lakshmana making all out efforts like Lord Visnu to kill the demons.

Shlok: द्रक्ष्यस्यद्वैव वैदेहि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्।

Translation: व्यवसायसमायुक्तं विष्णुं दैत्यवधे यथा।।
Mighty Rama staying in asram ill be enthused to see you seated on my back like Lord Purandara (Indra) seated on the back of the lord of elephants (Airavata)

Shlok: त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहमाश्रमस्थं महाबलम्।

Translation: पुरन्दरमिवासीनं नागराजस्य मूर्धनि।।
O god like lady climb up my back. Do not be reluctant. Join Rama just as Rohini unites with the Moon, O beautiful one

Shlok: पृष्ठमारोह मे देवि मा विकाङ्क्षस्व शोभने।

Translation: योगमन्विच्छ रामेण शशाङ्केनेव रोहिणी।।
O bull among monkeys you have such a small body. How can you intend to carry me from here to my husband, the lord of men?

Shlok: कथं वाल्पशरीरस्त्वं मामितो नेतुमिच्छसि।

Translation: सकाशं मानवेन्द्रस्य भर्तुर्मे प्लवगर्षभ।।
Hanuman, the foremost of the vanaras resembling mount Meru or Mandara stood there glowing like blazing fire in front of Sita.

Shlok: मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशो बभौ दीप्तानलप्रभः।

Translation: अग्रतो व्यवतस्थे च सीताया वानरोत्तमः।।
Resembling a mountain in size, with a red face, with teeth and nails strong like diamond, the vanara in dreadful form said to Vaidehi:

Shlok: हरिः पर्वतसङ्काशस्ताम्रवक्त्रो महाबलः।

Translation: वज्रदंष्ट्रनखो भीमो वैदेहीमिदमब्रवीत्।।
Seeing the son of Maruta in dreadful form, the broad lotus petaleyed daughter of Janaka with eyes as large as lotus petals replied :

Shlok: तं दृष्ट्वा भीमसङ्काशमुवाच जनकात्मजा।

Translation: पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षी मारुतस्यौरसं सुतम्।।
O great monkey I have understood your strength and power. Your speed is like the Windgod's and your power is astonishing and splendid.

Shlok: तव सत्त्वं बलं चैव विजानामि महाकपे।

Translation: वायोरिव गतिं चैव तेजश्चाग्नेरिवाद्भुतम्।।

Shlok: यदि रामो दशग्रीवमिह हत्त्वा सबान्धवम्।

Translation: मामितो गृह्य गच्छेत तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्।।
After seeing Rama who is equal to lord Indra in valour. He is like blazing fire whipped by wind, wielding a wonderful bow, who can withstand the power of strong Rama accompanied by Lakshmana in war?
Shlok: समीक्ष्य तं संयति चित्रकार्मुकम् महाबलं वासवतुल्यविक्रमम्।

Translation: सलक्ष्मणं को विषहेत राघवं हुताशनं दीप्तमिवानिलेरितम्।।

O chief of vanaras who can withstand Rama accompanied by Lakshmana, the conqueror of enemies? His arrows resemble the rays of the Sun at the time of the deluge, steady like the elephants who support the quarters of the earth.

Shlok: सलक्ष्मणं राघवमाजिमर्दनं दिशागजं मत्तमिव व्यवस्थितम्।

Translation: सहेत को वानरमुख्य संयुगे युगान्तसूर्यप्रतिमं शरार्चिषम्।
Having heard Hanuman, Sita, a child of god, said these words in a low tone. Choked with tears, 'Carry this token of identity to my dear husband':

Shlok: एवमुक्ता हनुमता सीता सुरसुतोपमा।

Translation: उवाच वचनं मन्दं बाष्पप्रग्रथिताक्षरम्।।
O strongarmed Rama, seeing my torn breasts, you became angry like a hissing serpent and hissing said
Shlok: स मां दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्वितुन्नां स्तनयोस्तदा।।5.38.25।।

Translation: आशीविष इव क्रुद्धश्वसन्वाक्यमभाषत।
O Sita with a beautiful lap like an elephant trunk by whom is your bosom wounded? Who is sporting with an angry fivehooded snake?

Shlok: केन ते नागनासोरु विक्षतं वै स्तनान्तरम्।।5.38.26।।

Translation: कः क्रीडति सरोषेण पञ्चवक्त्रेण भोगिना।

Taking out a blade of darbha grass from your mat, you invoked the weapon of Brahma by reciting the mantra. Then you discharged it which blazed like the fire of death and went spearheading towards the crow.

Shlok: स दर्भं संस्तराद्गृह्य ब्राह्मेणास्त्रेण योजयत्।।5.38.30।।

Translation: स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्जज्वालाभिमुखो द्विजम्।
O bull among men you are so loving to me. I am like an orphan. Be kind to me. She who has found her lord in you stays without a protector.

Shlok: स कुरुष्व महोत्साहः कृपां मयि नरर्षभ।

Translation: त्वया नाथवती नाथ ह्यनाथा इव दृश्यते।।

O my supreme lord I know you are kind, righteous, valiant, vigroous, mighty. You are boundless, calm and deep like the ocean. You are lord of earth and the seas and compeer of Vasava. I have heard from you that motiveless compassion is the best way to make one righteous.
Shlok: अपारपारमक्षोभ्यं गाम्भीर्यात्सागरोपमम्।

Translation: भर्तारं ससमुद्राया धरण्या वासवोपमम्।।
Hanuman having spoken this way, Sita, resembling a god's daughter, grieving, thus addressed Hanuman:

Shlok: इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंस्तु सीता सुरसुतोपमा।

Translation: उवाच शोकसन्तप्ता हनुमन्तं प्लवङ्गमम्।।

Heroic Lakshmana, did not know while I was borne away. He is prosperous, foremost in serving elders. He is energetic and reserved in his speech like my fatherinlaw. He is a prince dear (to his brother).

Shlok: वृद्धोपसेवी लक्ष्मीवान् शक्तो न बहुभाषिता।।5.38.61।।

Translation: राजपुत्रः प्रियः श्रेष्ठः सदृशः श्वशुरस्य मे।
O heroic Rama just as Kausik was rescued from the underworld it behoves you to deliver me from imprisonment of wicked Ravana".

Shlok: रावणेनोपरुद्धां मां निकृत्य पापकर्मणा।

Translation: त्रातुमर्हसि वीर त्वं पातालादिव कौशिकीम्।।
Having received the most precious jewel from the daughter of Janaka, Hanuman prepared to return like a mountain released from the impact of the wind.
Shlok: मणिवरमुपगृह्य तं महार्हं जनकनृपात्मजया धृतं प्रभावात्।

Translation: गिरिरिव पवनावधूतमुक्तः सुखितमनाः प्रतिसङ्क्रमं प्रपेदे।।
Both the valiant Rama and Lakshmana, lions among men, looking brilliant like Sun and Moon will come to you riding on my back.

Shlok: मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ।

Translation: त्वत्सकाशं महासत्त्वौ नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः।।
Therefore, count the days and rest assured. Let it be auspicious to you. You will shortly see Rama burning like fire.

Shlok: तदाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते भव त्वं कालकाङ्क्षिणी।

Translation: नचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसे रामं प्रज्वलन्तमिवानलम्।।
When Ravana is slain, with his sons, ministers and kith and kin, you will reunite with
Rama as Rohini unites with the Moon.

Shlok: निहते राक्षसेन्द्रेऽस्मिन्सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवे।

Translation: त्वं समेष्वसि रामेण शशाङ्केनेव रोहिणी।।
You will soon see heroic vanaras whose weapons are their teeth, who are like lion and tiger in their valour. They are (mighty) like wellbred elephants.

Shlok: नखदंष्ट्रायुधान्वीरान्सिम्हशार्दूलविक्रमान्।

Translation: वानरान्वारणेन्द्राभान्क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि सङ्गतान्।।
O respectable lady you would see many troops of vanara chiefs who resemble clouds hovering on the mountain peaks of Lankaroaring.

Shlok: शैलाम्बुदनिकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु।

Translation: नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानामार्ये यूधान्यनेकशः।।
Rama is tormented by the dreadful arrows of the god of love pierced into vitals, like an elephant hit by a lion. He has no happiness in life.

Shlok: स तु मर्मणि घोरेण ताडितो मन्मथेषुणा।

Translation: न शर्म लभते रामस्सिंहार्धित इव द्विपः।।
Who is superior to Rama? Who is equal to Lakshmana? Both the brothers are like Fire and Wind. They are your refuge.

Shlok: रामाद्विशिष्टः कोऽन्योऽस्ति कश्चित्सौमित्रिणा समः।

Translation: अग्निमारुतकल्पौ तौ भ्रातरौ तव संश्रयौ।।
Both the valiant Rama and Lakshmana, lions among men, looking brilliant like Sun and Moon will come to you riding on my back.
Shlok: मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ।

Translation: त्वत्सकाशं महासत्त्वौ नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः।।
Therefore, count the days and rest assured. Let it be auspicious to you. You will shortly see Rama burning like fire.

Translation: नचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसे रामं प्रज्वलन्तमिवानलम्।।
When Ravana is slain, with his sons, ministers and kith and kin, you will reunite with
Rama as Rohini unites with the Moon.
Shlok: निहते राक्षसेन्द्रेऽस्मिन्सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवे।

Translation: त्वं समेष्वसि रामेण शशाङ्केनेव रोहिणी।।
You will soon see heroic vanaras whose weapons are their teeth, who are like lion and tiger in their valour. They are (mighty) like wellbred elephants.
Shlok: नखदंष्ट्रायुधान्वीरान्सिम्हशार्दूलविक्रमान्।

Translation: वानरान्वारणेन्द्राभान्क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि सङ्गतान्।।
Rama is tormented by the dreadful arrows of the god of love pierced into vitals, like an elephant hit by a lion. He has no happiness in life.
Shlok: स तु मर्मणि घोरेण ताडितो मन्मथेषुणा।

Translation: न शर्म लभते रामस्सिंहार्धित इव द्विपः।।
O devi weep no more.Entertain no unpleasant thoughts.You have a great husband, just as Sachi has her lord Indra.

Shlok: मा रुदो देवि शोकेन माभूत्ते मनसोऽप्रियम्।

Translation: शचीव पत्या शक्रेण भर्त्रा नाथवती ह्यसि।।
Who is superior to Rama? Who is equal to Lakshmana? Both the brothers are like Fire and Wind. They are your refuge.

Shlok: रामाद्विशिष्टः कोऽन्योऽस्ति कश्चित्सौमित्रिणा समः।

Translation: अग्निमारुतकल्पौ तौ भ्रातरौ तव संश्रयौ।।
Sita who was like the daughter of the gods heard the son of the Windgod for her benefit and replied:

Shlok: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य वायुसूनोर्महात्मनः।

Translation: उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं सीता सुरसुतोपमा।।
Be kind to me and act in such a manner that I may embrace my lord passionately with
my body emaciated with grief.
Shlok: यथा तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गात्रैश्शोकाभिकर्शितैः।

Translation: संस्पृशेयं सकामाहं तथा कुरु दयां मयि।।
Rama you are like Indra and Varuna in valiance. How are you tolerating Sita seized, dwelling among the demons?

Shlok: स वीर्यवान्कथं सीतां हृतां समनुमन्यसे।

Translation: वसन्तीं रक्षसां मध्ये महेन्द्रवरुणोपमः।।
O sinless Rama this wonderful Chudamani of mine has been carefully safeguarded. Seeing this is like seeing you when I am in distress.
Shlok: एष चूडामणिर्दिव्यो मया सुपरिरक्षितः।

Translation: एतं दृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्यामि व्यसने त्वामिवानघ।।
O Hanuman to the lionlike brothers Rama and Lakshmana, to Sugriva including his ministers and to every one convey my good wishes.
Shlok: हनुमन्सिंहसङ्काशौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।

Translation: सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान् ब्रूयाह्यनामयम्।।
This Ashoka garden of Ravana filled with different kinds of trees and creepers is a feast to the eyes and mind. It is an excellent garden like the Nandana garden of Indra.

Shlok: इदमस्य नृशंसस्य नन्दनोपममुत्तमम्।

Translation: वनं नेत्रमनःकान्तं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्।।
I will devastate this garden, just as fire destroys a dried up forest. This will enrage Ravana.

Shlok: इदं विध्वंसयिष्यामि शुष्कं वनमिवानलः।

Translation: अस्मिन्भग्ने ततः कोपं करिष्यति दशाननः।।

Shlok: ततो मारुतवत्कृद्धो मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः।

Translation: ऊरुवेगेन महता द्रुमान्क्षेप्तुमथारभत्।।

Vines and trees wilted, birds shrieking, the embankments of ponds destroyed, its tender coppery red shoots withered, the garden looked as though it is burnt by forest fire and the climbers looked like women shivering in fear with their robes disarrayed.
Shlok: नानाशकुन्तविरुतैः प्रभिन्नैस्सलिलाशयैः।

Translation: ताम्रैः किसलयैः क्लान्तै: क्लान्तद्रुमलतायुतम्।।5.41.17।।
न बभौ तद्वनं तत्र दावानलहतं यथा।
व्याकुलावरणा रेजुर्विह्वला इव ता लताः।।5.41.18।।
Then, seeing the huge body of the mighty vanara resembling a mountain the ogresses questioned Janaki about him.
Shlok: ततस्तं गिरिसङ्काशमतिकायं महाबलम्।

Translation: राक्षस्यो वानरं दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छुर्जनकात्मजाम्।।5.42.5।।
On listening to the report of the ogresses, Ravana, the lord of demons flared up like blazing flame of a sacrificial fire, his eyeballs rolling in rage.

Shlok: राक्षसीनां वचश्त्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।

Translation: हुताग्निरिव जज्वाल कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः।।5.42.22।।
From his angry eyes fell down drops of tears just as burning drops of oil drip from two burning lamps.

Shlok: तस्य क्रुद्धस्य नेत्राभ्यां प्रापतन्नास्रबिन्दवः।

Translation: दीप्ताभ्यामिव दीपाभ्यां सार्चिष स्स्नेहबिन्दवः।।5.42.23।।
The kinkaras rushed towards the leader of vanaras who stood near the archway like the moths rushing towards the flame.
Shlok: ते कपीन्द्रं समासाद्य तोरणस्थमवस्थितम्।

Translation: अभिपेतुर्महावेगाः पतङ्गा इव पावकम्।।5.42.27।।
They assailed Hanuman with iron maces, crowbars edged with gold and shining arrows resembling the Sun.
Shlok: ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः परिघैः काञ्चनाङ्गदैः।

Translation: आजघ्नुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं शरैश्चादित्यसन्निभैः।।5.42.28।।
Gigantic Hanuman, illustrious and brilliant, roared and waved his tail striking it with force on the ground causing loud sound.
Shlok: हनुमानपि तेजस्वी श्रीमान्पर्वतसन्निभः।

Translation: क्षितावाविध्य लाङ्गूलं ननाद च महास्वनम्।।5.42.30।।
Terrified on hearing the roar, the kinkaras looked at the towering Hanuman who seemed like a cloud in twilight (red in colour).
Shlok: तस्य सन्नादशब्देन तेऽभवन्भयशङ्किताः।

Translation: ददृशुश्च हनूमन्तं सन्ध्यामेघमिवोन्नतम्।।5.42.37।।
Then Hanuman, son of the Windgod, decided in his mind to show his strength and jumped on to the top of the palatial building that appeared like the peak of mount Meru.
Shlok: चैत्यप्रासादमाप्लुत्य मेरुशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्।

Translation: आरुरोह कपिश्रेष्ठो हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः।।5.43.3।।
The powerful vanara leader climbed the tall, palatial building which resembled a mountain. He looked like another Sun, just risen.
Shlok: आरुह्य गिरिसङ्काशं प्रासादं हरियूथपः।

Translation: बभौ स सुमहातेजाः प्रतिसूर्य इवोदितः।।5.43.4।।

Having destroyed the fine palace building, the indomitable Hanuman was blazing with glory like the mountain Pariyatra. (one of the seven Kula mountains viz., Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Shuktiman, Riksha, Vindhya and Pariyatra)
Shlok: संप्रधृष्य च दुर्धर्षं चैत्यप्रासादमुत्तमम्।

Translation: हनुमान्प्रज्वलन्लक्ष्म्या पारियात्रोपमोऽभवत्।।5.43.5।।
Holding astonishing maces decorated with gold, iron crowbars and sharp arrows resembling the rays of the Sun the ogres hit Hanuman, the foremost of vanaras.

Shlok: आजघ्नुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं बाणैश्चादित्यसन्निभैः। आवर्त इव गङ्गायास्तोयस्य विपुलो महान्।।5.43.14

Translation: Thereafter fire was generated (through friction) and with if the palace blazed. Hanuman saw the palace burning. He killed a hundred demons there as Indra killed demons with his thunderbolt. (The whirling pillar that generated fire apeared like a thunderbolt) Later he stood in the air and proclaimed this:
Shlok: दह्यमानं ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रासादं हरियूथपः।

Translation: स राक्षसशतं हत्त्वा वज्रेणेन्द्र इवासुरान्।।5.43.19।।
His red face struck by an arrow appeared like a fullblown lotus in autumn season hit by the rays of the Sun.
Shlok: तस्य तच्छुशुभे ताम्रं शरेणाभिहतं मुखम्।

Translation: शरदीवाम्बुजं फुल्लं विद्धं भास्कररश्मिना।।5.44.8।।
His red face stained with blood was glowing bright like red lotus in the sky sprinkled with drops of red sandal.
Shlok: तत्तस्य रक्तं रक्तेन रञ्जितं शुशुभे मुखम्।

Translation: यथाकाशे महापद्मं सिक्तं चन्दनबिन्दुभिः।।5.44.9।।

Commanded by Ravana, the seven sons of minister blazing like fire followed by large army of experts in archery, possessing great valour, armed with weapons, being distinguished wielders of weapons, skilled in the use of weapons, who were equally capable of conquering each other sallied forth gladly to fight with Hanuman.
Shlok: ततस्ते राक्षसेन्द्रेण चोदिता मन्त्रिणस्सुताः।

Translation: निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्सप्तसप्तार्चिवर्चसः।।5.45.1।।

The valiant heroes were sporting and making sounds like stormy clouds wielding wonderful bows glittering like molten gold, shining like lightning. As they marched from the palace they looked like stormy clouds accompanied by lightning.
Shlok: तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि चापान्यमितविक्रमाः।  विस्फारयन्तस्संहृष्टास्तटित्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः।।5.45.4।।

Translation: They went roaring with their chariots rattling, sending forth torrents of arrows like the stormy clouds thundering.
Shlok: सृजन्तो बाणवृष्टिं ते रथगर्जितनिस्स्वनाः।

Translation: वृष्टिमन्त इवांभोदा विचेरुर्नैऋताम्बुदाः।।5.45.7।।
Later, Hanuman covered with showers of arrows scattered all over appeared like the king of mountains shot with showers of rain.
Shlok: अवकीर्णस्ततस्ताभिर्हनुमान्शरवृष्टिभिः।

Translation: अभवत्संवृताकारश्शैलराडिव वृष्टिभिः।।5.45.8।।
Sporting in the sky with the giants who held bows in their hands, Hanuman shone like the powerful Windgod sporting in the sky surrrounded by rambling dark clouds.

Shlok: स तैः क्रीडन्धनुष्मद्भिर्व्योम्नि वीरः प्रकाशते।

Translation: धनुष्मद्भिर्यथा मेघैर्मारुतः प्रभुरम्बरे।।5.45.10।।
The heroic giants caught sight of the vanara, who was blazing encircled as though he
was by the rays of his own glory, looking like the rising Sun. He was endowed with extraordinary agility, intelligence, and tremendous strength standing, waiting at the archway.

Shlok: रश्मिमन्तमिवोद्यन्तं स्वतेजोरश्मिमालिनम्।

Translation: तोरणस्थं महोत्साहं महासत्त्वं महाबलम्।।5.46.20।।

Durdhara pierced into the head of Hanuman with five sharp arrows and polished steel shafts with yellow tips (gold) shining like red lotus petals. They were like petals of lilies thrown on the head of Hanuman (causing no pain).
Shlok: तस्य पञ्चायसास्तीक्ष्णाश्शिताः पीतमुखाश्शराः।

Translation: शिरस्युत्पलपत्राभा दुर्धरेण निपातिताः।।5.46.22।।
The great monkey kept away the showering arrows like the wind prevents raincloud from showering rain drops at the end of monsoon.

Shlok: स कपिर्वारयामास तं व्योम्नि शरवर्षिणम्।

Translation: वृष्टिमन्तं पयोदान्ते पयोदमिव मारुतः।।5.46.25।।
The vanara pitted horses against horses, elephants against elephants, warriors against warriors and chariots against chariots as Indra destroyed demons.

Shlok: अश्वैरश्वान् गजैर्नागान् योधैर्योधान् रथैरथान्।।5.46.39।।

Translation: स कपिर्नाशयामास सहस्राक्ष इवासुरान्।

Then the heroic monkey having killed the army generals and their army and destroyed their vehicles in war came back to the archway after reviewing and stood like the timespirit bent upon the destruction of humanity.
Shlok: ततः कपिस्तान्ध्वजिनीपतीन् रणे निहत्य वीरान्सबलान्सवाहनान्।

Translation: समीक्ष्य वीरः परिगृह्य तोरणं कृतक्षणः काल इव प्रजाक्षये।।5.46.41।।

Spurred by the mere glance of Ravana, the glorious Aksha with his wonderful bow inlaid with gold sprang up from the royal assembly just as flame rises from firesanctuary when oblations are poured in by reputed brahmins.

Shlok: स तस्य दृष्ट्यर्पणसम्प्रचोदितः प्रतापवान्काञ्चनचित्रकार्मुकः।

Translation: समुत्पपाताथ सदस्युदीरितो द्विजातिमुख्यैर्हविषेव पावकः।।5.47.2।।
Ascending a glittering chariot inlaid with pure gold Aksha, the courageous bull among giants looking splendid like the rising Sun, marched forth towards the great vanara.

Shlok: ततो महद्बालदिवाकरप्रभं प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालसन्ततम्।

Translation: रथं समास्थाय ययौ स वीर्यवान्महाहरिं तं प्रति नैरृतर्षभः।।5.47.3।।

(The chariot) was unassailable to suras or asuras.It moved without touching the ground, it could fly in air and had the splendour of the Sun. It was equipped readily with quivers, eight swords, javelins and clubs placed in right order.

Shlok: सुरासुराधृष्यमसङ्गचारिणं रविप्रभं व्योमचरं समाहितम्।

Translation: सतूणमष्टासिनिबद्धबन्धुरं यथाक्रमावेशितशक्तितोमरम्।।5.47.5।।

Prince Aksha, whose courage was equal to that of gods, shone like the Sun. He ascended the splendid chariot decked with golden garlands shining like Sun and Moon, equipped with all weapons, bows and shields etc, he went out.

Shlok: विराजमानं प्रतिपूर्णवस्तुना सहेमदाम्ना शशिसूर्यवर्चसा।

Translation: दिवाकराभं रथमास्थितस्ततस्स निर्जगामामरतुल्यविक्रमः।।5.47.6।।
The lioneyed Aksha saw the vanara who appeared like the cosmic fire at the time of dissolution of the universe. The prince was astonished and struck with awe (at the
majestic form of the Vanara) and looked at him with great respect.

Shlok: स तं समासाद्य हरिं हरीक्षणो युगान्तकालाग्निमिव प्रजाक्षये।

Translation: अवस्थितं विस्मितजातसम्भ्रम स्समैक्षताक्षो बहुमानचक्षुषा।।5.47.8।।

Aksha, the mighty prince judging the speed and prowess of the monkey with his own in confronting enemies and the strength of the monkey, began to swell up in spirit like the glow of the Sun at the end of winter.

Shlok: स तस्य वेगं च कपेर्महात्मनः पराक्रमं चारिषु पार्थिवात्मजः।  विचारयन्स्वं च बलं महाबलो हिमक्षये सूर्य इवाभिवर्धते।।5.47.9।।

Translation: With the three arrows shot on his forehead simultaneously his eyes were drenched with flowing blood and with arrows shining like rays he appeared like the rising Sun, garlanded by glowing rays.
Shlok: स तै श्शरैर्मूर्ध्नि समं निपातितैः क्षरन्नसृग्दिग्धविवृत्तलोचनः।

Translation: नवोदितादित्यनिभ श्शरांशुमान् व्यराजतादित्य इवांशुमालिकः।।5.47.15।।

Huge Hanuman, endowed with strength and valour looked like the rising Sun on the peak of mount Mandara. He looked at prince Aksha and his army as well as his vehicles as though he was burning them with the rays emerging from his fiery eyes.
Shlok: स मन्दराग्रस्थ इवांशुमालिको विवृद्धकोपो बलवीर्यसंयुतः।

Translation: कुमारमक्षं सबलं सवाहनं ददाह नेत्राग्निमरीचिभिस्तदा।।5.47.17।।
Aksha, with his wonderful quiver and bow, began to rain rapidly a shower of arrows in the battle, on the mountainlike monkeylord just as a cloud rains on a mountain.

Shlok: ततस्स बाणासनचित्रकार्मुक श्शरप्रवर्षो युधि राक्षसाम्बुदः।

Translation: शरान्मुमोचाशु हरीश्वराचले वलाहको वृष्टिमिवाचलोत्तमे।।5.47.18।।
Young Aksha, proud of his valour with eyes bloodshot in anger rushed towards the matchless Hanuman, just as an elephant would approach a huge pitfall covered with grass.
Shlok: स बालभावाद्युधि वीर्यदर्पितः प्रवृद्धमन्युः क्षतजोपमेक्षणः।

Translation: समाससादाप्रतिमं कपिं रणे गजो महाकूपमिवावृतं तृणैः।।5.47.20।।

Mounted on a chariot, the mighty and glorious Aksa, the most distinguished of ogres and the most eminent of chariot-warriors, closely followed Hanuman even as the latter sprang up in the sky, covering him with shafts, even as a cloud would cover a mountain with showers of hailstones.
Shlok: समुत्पतन्तं समभिद्रवद्बली स राक्षसानां प्रवरः प्रतापवान्।

Translation: रथी रथिश्रेष्ठतमः किरन्शरैः पयोधरश्शैलमिवाश्मवृष्टिभिः।।5.47.22।।

Dodging like the wind between the arrows and also escaping the arrows Hanuman, who was swift in movement like the mind, was seen exhibiting his terrific valour in the battle while he moved in the sky.
Shlok: स तान्शरांस्तस्य हरिर्विमोक्षयंश्चचार वीरः पथि वायुसेविते।

Translation: शरान्तरे मारुतवद्विनिष्पतन्मनोजवस्संयति चण्डविक्रमः।।5.47.23।।

(Aksha) the great charioteer abandoned the chariot, held a sword and a bow, and flew up to the region of the sky with his fierce power just as a sage with his fearsome ascetic power ascends to heaven, leaving his body.

Shlok: स तं परित्यज्य महारथो रथं सकार्मुकः खङ्गधरः खमुत्पतन्।

Translation: तपोऽभियोगादृषिरुग्रवीर्यवान्विहाय देहं मरुतामिवालयम्।।5.47.33।।
Thereupon Hanuman with the prowess that was equal to wind, approaching the sky firmly caught hold of the legs of Aksha flying into the abode of Garuda, the Windgod and the Siddhas.
Shlok: ततः कपिस्तं विचरन्तमम्बरे पतत्रिराजानिलसिद्धसेविते।

Translation: समेत्य तं मारुततुल्यविक्रमः क्रमेण जग्राह स पादयोर्दृढम्।।5.47.34।।

Hanuman, the foremost of the vanaras who was equal to his father in valour, seized him just as Garuda, the lord of birds, would seize a great serpent. And spinning him round speedily a thousand times and hitting him, dropped him on the earth.

Shlok: स तं समाविध्य सहस्रशः कपिर्महोरगं गृह्य इवाण्डजेश्वरः।

Translation: मुमोच वेगात्पितृतुल्यविक्रमो महीतले संयति वानरोत्तमः।।5.47.35।।

Hanuman, the hero with bloodshot eyes having slain Aksha, shone resplendent like the son of Indra (Jayanta), and reached the portal, and waited looking like the god of death determined to destroy all beings.
Shlok: निहत्य तं वज्रिसुतोपमप्रभं कुमारमक्षं क्षतजोपमेक्षणम्।  तमेव वीरोऽभिजगाम तोरणं कृतक्षणः काल इव प्रजाक्षये।।5.47.38।।

Translation: The power of your penance, your valour and your ability to discharge astras in war is equal only to mine. I am not bothered about the consequences of war you wage because your victory is certain.

Shlok: ममानुरूपं तपसो बलं च ते पराक्रमश्चास्त्रबलं च संयुगे।

Translation: न त्वां समासाद्य रणावमर्दे मनश्श्रमं गच्छति निश्चितार्थम्।।5.48.6।।

O warrior of extraordinary merit among the wielders of astras asses your strength approach the enemy in a manner by which he is subdued without causing further destruction to our army. Carefully measure your own strength and your enemy's before you start fighting.

Shlok: बलावमर्थस्तयि सन्निकृष्टे यथा गते शाम्यति शान्तशत्रौ।

Translation: तथा समीक्ष्यात्मबलं परं च समारभस्वास्त्रविदां वरिष्ठ।।5.48.10।।
When the illustrious son of Ravana, the highly Indrajit resplendent with eyes of lotus petals marched ahead he looked like the turbulent ocean on a fullmoon day.

Shlok: श्रीमान्पद्मपलाशाक्षो राक्षसाधिपतेस्सुतः।

Translation: निर्जगाम महातेजास्समुद्र इव पर्वसु।।5.48.17।।

Like Indra, Indrajit ascended the chariot (which had the standard of Indra as it was seized from him as a token of his having conquered Indra) yoked to four sharptoothed tigers. It moved in swiftness vying with Garuda, the king of birds in speed.
Shlok: स पक्षिराजोपमतुल्यवेगैर्व्याळैश्चतुर्भिः सिततीक्षणदंष्ट्रैः।

Translation: रथं समायुक्तमसहयवेगं समारुरोहेन्द्रजिदिन्द्रकल्पः।।5.48.18।।
Then the son of the demon king and Hanuman, both very fast in speed, mighty and powerful, fearless in war and like sura and asura closed in upon each other.

Shlok: ततस्समेतावतितीक्ष्णवेगौ महाबलौ तौ रणनिर्विशङ्कौ।

Translation: कपिश्च रक्षोधिपतेस्तनूजः सुरासुरेन्द्राविव बद्धवैरौ।।5.48.26।।

The demon did not find a way to hit Hanuman. Maruti also found no opportunity to hit great Indrajit. Both of them being equal to gods in valour became too much to each other in war. (Both of them moved at meteoric speed making it difficult to aim at the enemy.)
Shlok: हनुमतो वेद न राक्षसोऽन्तरं न मारुतिस्तस्य महात्मनोऽन्तरम्।

Translation: परस्परं निर्विषहौ बभूवतुः समेत्य तौ देवसमानविक्रमौ।।5.48.33।।
The ogres presented the best of monkeys, Hanuman looking like an elephant in rut to Ravana, the demon king.
Shlok: तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं बद्धं कपिवरोत्तमम्।

Translation: राक्षसा राक्षसेन्द्राय रावणाय न्यवेदयन्।।5.48.54।।
Hanuman the best of monkeys also saw the demon king who had both splendour and strength, radiating brilliance like the Sun.
Shlok: राक्षसाधिपतिं चापि ददर्श कपिसत्तमः।

Translation: तेजोबलसमायुक्तं तपन्तमिव भास्करम्।।5.48.59।।

He appeared terrible with bloodred eyes, shining sharp big teeth, drooping lips and ten heads, which looked like ten peaks of mountain Mandara inhabited by various beasts. He was heroic, powerful and splendid.
Shlok: शिरोभिर्दशभिर्वीरं भ्राजमानं महौजसम्।

Translation: नानाव्यालसमाकीर्णैश्शिखरैरिव मन्दरम्।।5.49.6।।

He was like a black mountain of collyrium, and with a face like the fullmoon. With a pearl necklace illumining his chest he appeared like a cloud lit up by the fullmoon with white cranes flying across. (The white pearlnecklace moving on his chest appeared like a row of cranes flying through the black cloud.)
Shlok: नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यं हारेणोरसि राजता।

Translation: पूर्णचन्द्राभवक्त्रेण सबलाकमिवाम्बुदम्।।5.49.7।।

He was attended by Durdhara, Prahasta, Mahaparsva and Nikumbha who were his learned ministers. Seated comfortably and attended by the four arrogant ministers, he was puffed with pride of their strength and appeared like the entire world surrounded by four oceans.

Shlok: सुखोपविष्टं रक्षोभिश्चतुर्भिर्बलदर्पितैः।

Translation: कृत्स्नं परिवृतं लोकं चतुर्भिरिव सागरैः।।5.49.12।।
He was attended by ogres including ministers who were intellectuals and adept in counselling. He appeared like lord Indra attended by the gods.

Shlok: मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रतत्त्वज्ञैरन्यैश्च शुभबुद्धिभिः।

Translation: अन्वास्यमानं रक्षोभिः सुरैरिव सुरेश्वरम्।।5.49.13।।
Hanuman saw the highly resplendent giant king (seated on the throne) who appeared like a cloud laden with water appearing on the peak of mount Meru.

Shlok: अपश्यद्राक्षसपतिं हनुमानतितेजसम्।

Translation: विष्ठितं मेरुशिखरे सतोयमिव तोयदम्।।5.49.14।।
There was an emperor named Dasaratha richly endowed with chariots, horses and elephants. He was a friend to the world and was like a father and equal to Indra in splendour.
Shlok: राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान्।

Translation: पितेव बन्धुर्लोकस्य सुरेश्वरसमद्युतिः।।5.51.4।।
Some of the very powerful heroes equal to Garuda, equal to the Windgod (in swiftness) have gone (in quest of Sita) without touching the earth.
Shlok: वैनतेयसमाः केचित्केचित्तत्रानिलोपमाः।

Translation: असङ्गगतयशशीघ्रा हरिवीरा महाबलाः।।5.51.14।।
I have seen Sita immersed in deep sorrow. You do not realise that by abducting her you are keeping a fivehooded female serpent in your house.
Shlok: लक्षितेयं मया सीता तथा शोकपरायणा।

Translation: गृह्य यां नाभिजानासि पञ्चास्यामिव पन्नगीम्।।5.51.23।।

Heroic Ravana there is hardly any one who is equal to you in the knowledge of dharma, in the practice of worldly affairs and in grasping subtle truths of sastras. Indeed you are supreme among suras and asuras.
Shlok: न धर्मवादे न च लोकवृत्ते न शास्त्रबुद्धिग्रहणेषु चापि।

Translation: विद्येत कश्चित्तव वीर तुल्य स्त्वंह्युत्तमस्सर्वसुरासुराणाम्।।5.52.17।।
While the tail was being swathed, the great vanara grew in size like wild fire fed with dry firewood.

Shlok: संवेष्ट्यमाने लाङ्गूले व्यवर्धत महाकपिः।

Translation: शुष्कमिन्धनमासाद्य वनेष्विव हुताशनः।।5.53.7।।
not found in gita press 5.53.21
Shlok: गृहांश्च मेघसङ्काशान् ददर्श पवनात्मजः।

Translation: Distressed on hearing the news which was as cruel as her own abduction Sita started burning with grief and invoked the firegod.
Shlok: लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन स एष परिणीयते। श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं क्रूरमात्मापहरणोपमम्।।5.53.25।।

Translation: The Windgod accompanying Hanuman's firelit tail also blew cool like the wind from snow, to calm the mind of the divine lady.
Shlok: हनुमज्जनकश्चापि पुच्छानलयुतोऽनिलः।।5.53.32।।

Translation: ववौ स्वास्थ्यकरो देव्याः प्रालेयानिलशीतलः।
Then the illustrious Hanuman reached the entrance of the lofty city, which was like the peak of a mountain and turned away the demons.
Shlok: उत्पपाताथ वेगेन ननाद च महाकपिः। पुरद्वारं ततश्श्रीमान् शैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्।।5.53.40

Translation: From his mountainlike form he assumed his original small figure within a moment casting off the bonds.
Shlok: विभक्तरक्षस्सम्बाधमाससादानिलात्मजः। स भूत्वा शैलसङ्काशः क्षणेन पुनरात्मवान्।।5.53.41।।

Translation: Illustrious Hanuman was relieved of the bond and once again grew to a mountain size. Looking around he saw an iron club near the archway.

Shlok: ह्रस्वतां परमां प्राप्तो बन्धनान्यवशातयत्। विमुक्तश्चाभवछ्रचीमान् पुनः पर्वतसन्निभः।।5.53.42।।

Translation: Hanuman, who was of fearsome valour in war with the demons, having killed them, gazed at Lanka once again. Garlanded by the flames of his tail around, he shone like the Sun covered with garlands of rays.
Shlok: स तान्निहत्त्वा रणचण्डविक्रम स्समीक्षमाणः पुनरेव लङ्काम्।

Translation: प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलकृतार्चिमाली प्रकाशतादित्य इवार्चिमाली।।5.53.44।।
The great Hanuman, with his burning tail wandered on tops of the mansions of Lanka, which looked like clouds with lightning.

Shlok: ततः प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलस्सविद्युदिव तोयदः।

Translation: भवनाग्रेषु लङ्काया विचचार महाकपिः।।5.54.6।।

Powerful and brave Hanuman who was equal to the Windgod in speed jumped down on the house of Prahasta and set fire to it. From there he jumped on to Mahaparsva's house and set it ablaze. Hanuman appeared like the fireflame at the time of dissolution.

Shlok: ततोऽन्यत्पुप्लुवे वेश्म महापार्श्वस्य वीर्यवान्।

Translation: मुमोच हनुमानग्निं कालानलशिखोपमम्।।5.54.9।।

Then Hanuman, the hero with the burning tail set fire to the chief palace of Ravana that resembled mountains Meru and Mandara, decorated with different kinds of gems and exquisite with several auspicious articles. While the flames were rising up, he roared like the thundering cloud at the time of dissolution.
Shlok: ततस्तस्मिन्गृहे मुख्ये नानारत्नविभूषिते।

Translation: मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशे सर्वमङ्गळशोभिते।।5.54.19।।
प्रदीप्तमग्निमुत्सृज्य लाङ्गूलाग्रे प्रतिष्ठितम्।
ननाद हनुमान्वीरो युगान्तजलदो यथा।।5.54.20।।
The windgod's association made the fire spread at great speed. It appeared like fire at the time of dissolution.
Shlok: श्वसनेन च संयोगादतिवेगो महाबलः।

Translation: कालाग्निरिव जज्वाल प्रावर्धत हुताशनः।।5.54.21।।
They held their breastfeeding babies in their arms, their hair let loose shouting as they jumped. As they were alighting, they glowed like lightnings dropping from the clouds.
Shlok: पतन्त्यो रेजिरेऽभ्रेभ्यस्सौदामन्य इवाम्बरात्। वज्रविद्रुमवैदूर्यमुक्तारजतसंहितान्।।5.54.27।।

Translation: Just as fire is not satisfied with dry sticks and grass Hanuman was not satisfied with the dead demons.

Shlok: विचित्रान्भवनाद्धातून् स्यन्दमानान्ददर्श सः। नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां तृणानां च यथा तथा।5.54.28

Translation: Blessed indeed are the highsouled men, who in their wisdom restrain their own anger as one would put off burning fire with water.
Shlok: धन्यास्ते पुरुषश्रेष्ठा ये बुद्ध्या कोपमुत्थितम्।

Translation: निरुन्धन्ति महात्मानो दीप्तमग्निमिवाम्भसा।।5.55.3।।
A man who drives away his rising anger with tolerance just as a snake casts off its slough is alone called a truly wise man.
Shlok: यस्समुत्पतितं क्रोधं क्षमयैव निरस्यति।

Translation: यथोरगस्त्वचं जीर्णां स वै पुरुष उच्यते।।5.55.6।।
The city is crowded with women, children and old demons running (in a bid to save themselves). The loud wails of demons resounded in the mountaincaves. It was as if the city was shrieking loudly.

Shlok: प्रपलायितरक्षः स्त्रीबालवृद्धसमाकुला।

Translation: जनकोलाहलाध्माता क्रन्दन्तीवाद्रिकन्दरै: ।।5.55.31।।

Nay, this doubt ever stands before me, as it were, about your very mighty associate monkeys and bears, O hero, as to how on earth Sugriva (who is endowed with extraordinary might) or those hordes of monkeys and bears or those two princes will actually be able to cross over the sea, which is so difficult to accomplish.
Shlok: अयं च वीर संदेहस्तिष्ठतीव ममाग्रतः । सुमहत्सु सहायेषु हर्वृक्षेषु महाबलः ॥ 5.56.7॥

Translation: If Kakutstha Rama, the slayer of enemy forces comes to Lanka, fills it with his arrows and takes me back, it will be worthy of him.
Shlok: शरैस्तु सङ्कुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः।  मां नयेद्यदि काकुत्स्थस्तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्।।5.56.12।।

Translation: You should act in such a manner that the exalted Rama, who is chivalrous in the battlefield, exhibits his valour worthy of his stature
Shlok: तद्यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः।

Translation: भवत्याहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादय।।5.56.13।।

When Ravana, the lord of ogres, is slain along with his sons, ministers and kinsfolk, you shall be united with Sri Rama as Rohini (a consort of the moon-god presiding over a constellation of the same name) is with the moon-god.
Shlok: निहते राक्षसेन्द्रे च सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवे ।  त्वं समेष्यसि रामेण शशाङ्केनेव रोहिणी ॥ २०।।

Translation: As if the mountain was awakened from sleep by the rays of the blessed Sun. With the colour of glowing minerals exuding, it was as if the mountain was looking out with his eyes open.
Shlok: सोत्तरीयमिवाम्भोदैः शृंगान्तरविलम्बिभिः। बोध्यमानमिव प्रीत्या दिवाकरकरैश्शुभैः।।5.56.27।।

Translation: With the loud sounds of masses of gurgling waters, the mountain appeared as though
it was standing and reciting (the Vedas) loudly. With murmuring sounds of different waterfalls, it appeared as though the mountain was singing.
Shlok: उन्मिषन्तमिवोद्धूतैर्लोचनैरिव धातुभिः। तोयौघननिस्स्वनैर्मन्द्रैः प्राधीतमिव पर्वतम्।5.56.28

Translation: With the tall devadaru trees on the mountain, it appeared as if the sages were standing with shoulders lifted up and performing penance. The sounds of waterfalls filled all over with reverberations.

Shlok: प्रगीतमिव विस्पष्टैर्नानाप्रस्रवणस्वनैः। देवदारुभिरत्युच्चैरूर्ध्वबाहुमिव स्थितम्।5.56.29

Translation: The sounds of waterfalls filled all over with reverberations. The mountain appeared as if trembling with the dark clouds of autumn.
Shlok: प्रपातजलनिर्घोषैः प्राक्रुष्टमिव सर्वतः। वेपमानमिव श्यामैः कम्पमानैश्शरद्वनैः।5.56.30

Translation: The shrill sounds pasing through the hollow bamboos filled with air appeared as if it was producing sweet musical notes. The mountain was as though hissing like a dreadful, poisonous snake.
Shlok: वेणुभिर्मारुतोद्धूतैः कूजन्तमिव कीचकैः। निश्श्वसन्तमिवामर्षाद्घोरैराशीविषोत्तमैः।5.56.31

Translation: With the caves standing majestically covered with mist, the mountain appeared as if it was meditating. With the ranges of foothills appearing like the feet of clouds traversing, with its peaks like garlands of clouds traversing over the mountain, it made one feel it was yawning.

Shlok: नीहारकृतगम्भीरैर्ध्यायन्तमिव गह्वरैः। मेघपादनिभैः पादैः प्रक्रान्तमिव सर्वतः।5.56.32

Translation: With the ranges of foothills appearing like the feet of clouds traversing, with its peaks like garlands of clouds traversing over the mountain, it made one feel it was yawning.

Shlok: जृंम्भमाणमिवाऽकाशे शिखरैरभ्रमालिभिः। कूटैश्च बहुधा कीर्णैश्शोभितं बहुकन्दरैः।5.56.33

Translation: Then the heroic son of the Windgod, who had ascended the mountain saw the dreadful ocean inhabited by fishes and snakes. Hanuman, the tiger among monkeys leaped into the sky like the Windgod from the south to the north shore.
Shlok: ददर्श सागरं भीमं मीनोरगनिषेवितम्। स मारुत इवाऽकाशं मारुतस्यात्मसम्भवः।5.56.41

Translation: Shaken by the violent force of Hanuman's thighs, the blossoming trees fell on the
ground like sickmen hit by Indra's thunderbolt.
Shlok: तस्योरुवेगोन्मथिताः पादपाः पुष्पशालिनः।।5.56.44।।

Translation: निपेतुर्भूतले रुग्णाश्शक्रायुधहता इव।

Hanuman leaped ike the Windgod, unwearied across the sky, as a huge boat crosses an ocean. The ocean was graced with a swan, the sky with constellation of Swati with fullblown lotuses and water lilies, like the nagas, yakshas, and gandharvas gathered together. The Moon in the sky was like a white lotus.
Shlok: आप्लुत्य च महावेगः पक्षवानिव पर्वतः। भुजङ्गयक्षगन्धर्वप्रबुद्धकमलोत्पलम्।5.56.1

Translation: Great Hanuman, son of the Windgod, flew through the abode of the Windgod as if he was swallowing the space, scratching the Moon, lord of the stars, as if seizing the heavens along with the constellation of Sun and stars and as though he was drawing the clusters of clouds.

Shlok: ग्रसमान इवाकाशं ताराधिपमिवोल्लिखन्।

Translation: हरन्निव सनक्षत्रं गगनं सार्कमण्डलम्।।5.57.5।।
With his exist and entrances into the mass of clouds, his appearances and disappearances among the clouds, he looked like the Moon.
Shlok: प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः।

Translation: प्रच्छन्नश्च प्रकाशश्च चन्द्रमा इव लक्ष्यते।।5.57.8।।
Passing through the clouds, appearing and disappearing, the heroic Hanuman clad in white was like the Moon in the white sky.

Shlok: विविधाभ्रघनापन्नगोचरो धवलाम्बरः।(lupta?)  दृश्यादृश्यतनुर्वीरस्तदा चन्द्रायतेऽम्बरे।।5.57.9।।

Translation: As he made his way through flakes of clouds, again and again appearing and disappearing, Hanuman the delight of the Windgod shone in the sky roaring like a thundering cloud. He looked like Garuda.

Shlok: तार्क्ष्यायमाणो गगने बभासे वायुनन्दनः।

Translation: दारयन्मेघबृन्दानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः।।5.57.10।।
The valiant Hanuman touched the lord of mountains fondly and went with great speed just as an arrow released from the centre of a powerful bowstring.
Shlok: ज्यामुक्त इव नाराचो महावेगोऽभ्युपागतः। स किञ्चिदनुसम्प्राप्तः समालोक्य महागिरिम्।।5.57.14।।

Translation: The chief of the monkeys arrived near, and beholding the face of the Mahendra mountain, which resembled a mass of clouds, thundered.
Shlok: महेन्द्रं मेघसङ्काशं ननाद हरिपुङ्गवः।

Translation: स पूरयामास कपिर्दिशो दश समन्ततः।।5.57.15।।
By the terrific sounds made by Hanuman in joy, it seemed as though the pathway of Garuda, the sky along with the Sun's orbit was splitting.
Shlok: फलतीवास्य घोषेण गगनं सार्कमण्डलम्।

Translation: ये तु तत्रोत्तरे तीरे समुद्रस्य महाबलाः।।5.57.18।।

Thereafter the brave and powerful monkeys waiting on the northern shore of the ocean for the arrival of the son of the Windgod, heard the roar and thundering sound of the stormy cloud produced by the sweeping motion of Hanuman's thighs propelled by the speed of his movement.

Shlok: महतो वातनुन्नस्य तोयदस्येव गर्जितम्।।5.57.19।।

Translation: शुश्रुवुस्ते तदा घोषमूरुवेगं हनूमतः।
All the vanaras who were feeling dejected and waiting anxiously heard the noise of Hanuman that sounded like a thundering cloud.
Shlok: ते दीनमनसस्सर्वे शुश्रुवुः काननौकसः।।5.57.20।।

Translation: वानरेन्द्रस्य निर्घोषं पर्जन्यनिनदोपमम्।
Waiting for Hanuman, the vanaras jumped from the tree tops holding the branches. They shook the branches just like clothes to welcome friends.
वासांसीव प्रशाखाश्च समाविध्यन्त वानराः।
Hanuman, the powerful son of the Windgod roared like the wind captured in a mountain cave would.

Shlok: गिरिगह्वरसंलीनो यथा गर्जति मारुतः।।5.57.27।।

Translation: एवं जगर्ज बलवान् हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः।
(On seeing) Hanuman, who was resembling a heavy cloud approaching, the vanaras stood with folded hands.

Shlok: तमभ्रघनसङ्काशमापतन्तं महाकपिम्।।5.57.28।।

Translation: दृष्ट्वा ते वानरास्सर्वे तस्थुः प्राञ्जलयस्तदा।
Overwhelmed with immeasurable joy, Hanuman descended from the sky like the mountain with its wings cut off and dropped on the bank of a mountain stream.
Shlok: हर्षेणापूर्यमाणोऽसौ रम्ये पर्वतनिर्झरे।।5.57.30।।

Translation: छिन्नपक्ष इवाऽकाशात्पपात धरणीधरः।
Then hearing Hanuman's meaningful and nectarlike words all the vanaras rejoiced.

Shlok: उपवासपरिश्रान्ता जटिला मलिना कृशा।।5.57.40।। ततो दृष्टेति वचनं महार्थममृतोपमम्।

Translation: Some elephantlike vanaras who were excited and felt overjoyed lifted their long and beautiful tails and hit them on the ground. A few vanaras jumped down from the mountain top and hugged the elephantlike Hanuman.

Shlok: आयताञ्चितदीर्घाणि लाङ्गूलानि प्रविव्यधुः।।5.57.43।। अपरे च हनूमन्तं वानरा वारणोपमम्।

Translation: Surrounded by many great vanaras, Angada was shining like Indra, lord of the gods attended by the gods in heaven.
Shlok: तस्थौ तत्राङ्गदः श्रीमान् वानरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः।

Translation: उपास्यमानो विबुधैर्दिवि देवपतिर्यथा।।5.57.52।।
Even as I was leaping I saw a terrific and wonderful golden peak which came as if to obstruct me on my path.

Shlok: गच्छतश्च हि मे घोरं विघ्नरूपमिवाभवत्।

Translation: काञ्चनं शिखरं दिव्यं पश्यामि सुमनोहरम्।।5.58.9।।
Hit by my tail the great mountain peak, which was radiating like the Sun was shattered into a thousand pieces.

Shlok: शिखरं सूर्यसङ्काशं व्यशीर्यत सहस्रधा। व्यवसायं च तं बुद्ध्वा स होवाच महागिरिः।।5.58.12।

Translation: Perceiving that I am going to smash him he spoke to me in a sweet tone delighting my heart, addressing me like a son.
Shlok: पुत्रेति मधुरां वाणीं मनः प्रह्लादयन्निव। पितृव्यं चापि मां विद्धि सखायं मातरिश्वनः।।5.58.13।।

Translation: O subduer of enemiesI must make efforts to help Rama the foremost among the righteous, for I have received help (from your father) who is equal to Indra in valour'.

Shlok: रामो धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः।

Translation: एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य मैनाकस्य महात्मनः।।5.58.18।।
She too opened her mouth wide enough for my size. Seeing her distending her mouth, in a moment I became small equal to the size of thumb and came out.

Shlok: तद्दृष्ट्वा व्यादितं चास्यं ह्रस्वं ह्यकरवं वपुः।

Translation: तस्मिन्मुहूर्ते च पुनर्बभूवाङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः।।5.58.31।।
Then | sprang into the vast space like Garuda (the king of birds, the carrier of Lord Visnu). In the meantime my shadow was held fast; yet | perceived nothing.
Shlok: ततोऽन्तरिक्षं विपुलं प्लुतोऽहं गरुडो यथा। छाया मे निगृहीता च न च पश्यामि किंचन।।5.58.35।।

Translation: She who resembled a mountain fell into the ocean with her arms hanging down when I pulled out her heart.

Shlok: सा विसृष्टभुजा भीमा पपात लवणाम्भसि।

Translation: मया पर्वतसङ्काशा निकृत्तहृदया सती।।5.58.44।।

Not far from the Simsupa tree I saw beautiful Sita, of dark complexion, with eyes like lotus petals, whose face was emaciated due to fasting, wearing only a single sari (the same one since her abduction) her locks filled with dust, pathetic looking, immersed in sorrow, meditating on her husband seated like a doe encircled by tigresses, surrounded by ugly and cruel shedemons fed on flesh and blood.

Shlok: श्यामां कमलपत्राक्षीमुपवासकृशाननाम्।

Translation: तदेकवासस्संवीतां रजोध्वस्तशिरोरुहाम्।।5.58.57।।

Not far from the Simsupa tree I saw beautiful Sita, of dark complexion, with eyes like lotus petals, whose face was emaciated due to fasting, wearing only a single sari (the same one since her abduction) her locks filled with dust, pathetic looking, immersed in sorrow, meditating on her husband seated like a doe encircled by tigresses, surrounded by ugly and cruel shedemons fed on flesh and blood.

Shlok: मांसशोणितभक्षाभिर्व्याघ्रीभिर्हरिणीमिव।

Translation: सा मया राक्षसीमध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः।।5.58.59।।

Shlok: एकवेणीधरा दीना भर्तृचिन्तापरायणा।

Translation: भूमिशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे।।5.58.60।।
Feeling supremely anxious, | thereupon contracted my form and remained crouched like a bird on the SimSapa tree thick with foliage.
Shlok: ततोऽहं परमोद्विग्नः स्वं रूपं प्रत्यसंहरम्।

Translation: अहं तु शिंशुपावृक्षे पक्षीव गहने स्थितः।।5.58.64।।
You are not equal to Rama and not even fit to be his servant. He does yagnas and always abides in truth. He is valiant in war.
Shlok: अपहृत्याऽऽगतः पाप ते नादृष्टो महात्मना। न त्वं रामस्य सदृशो दास्येऽप्यस्य न युज्यसे।।5.58.73।।

Translation: Thus addressed harshly by Janaki, the tenheaded Ravana blazed up in anger suddenly like the flame of the funeral pyre.
Shlok: जज्वाल सहसा कोपाच्चितास्थ इव पावकः।

Translation: विवृत्य नयने क्रूरे मुष्टिमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम्।।5.58.75।।
What purpose of yours will be served by Sita, O lord, You, who are equal in prowess to the mighty Indra? Pray, revel with me today; Sita, the daughter of Janaka, is in no way superior to me.
Shlok: सीतया तव किं कार्यं महेन्द्रसमविक्रम। मया सह रमस्वाद्य मद्विशिष्टा न जानकी।।5.58.78

Translation: Janaki did not care for their words of threat, as though they were a blade of grass and of no use to her.

Shlok: तृणवद्भाषितं तासां गणयामास जानकी।।5.58.82।।

Translation: गर्जितं च तदा तासां सीतां प्राप्य निरर्थकम्।

f this proves to be otherwise, my life is to continue only for a month (two fortnights*). If Sri Rama does not appear within this period |, as such, shall have to die like one without a protector and Sri Rama, a scion of Kakutstha, will no longer be able to see me.’
Shlok: यद्यन्यथा भवेदेतद्द्वौ मासौ जीवितं मम।

Translation: न मां द्रक्ष्यति काकुत्स्थो म्रिये साहमनाथवत्।।5.58.108।।
Thereafter, I increased my body to the size of a mountain, intent on fighting and started destroying the pleasure garden.
Shlok: ततोऽवर्धत मे कायस्तदा पर्वतसन्निभः।

Translation: युद्धकाङ्क्षी वनं तच्च विनाशयितुमारभे।।5.58.110।।
o whom is this glory of the monkeys not already known, who seek the presence even of gods only when invited by the latter for help?’
Shlok: वानराणां प्रभावो हि न केन विदितः पुरा। (lupta?)  देवतानां सङ्काशं च ये गच्छन्ति निमन्त्रिताः।।5.58.142।।

Translation: This I was asked to tell you by the king of vanaras wishing your welfare'. 'Ravana then angrily looked at me as if to burn me.
Shlok: इति वानरराजस्त्वामाहेत्यभिहितो मया।

Translation: मामैक्षत ततः क्रुद्धश्चक्षुषा प्रदहन्निव।।5.58.143।।
Then I leaped to the entrance gate of the city without being perplexed. With my burning tail I set fire to the boundaries and towering mansions which looked like the world at the end of dissolution.

Shlok: पुच्छेन च प्रदीप्तेन तां पुरीं साट्टगोपुराम्।।5.58.158।।

Translation: दहाम्यहमसंभ्रान्तो युगान्ताग्निरिव प्रजाः।

In the wicked, Ravana's Ashoka garden under the Simsupa tree the noble lady Sita surrounded by ogresses, is sitting, tormented by tears. Her brightness is like the Moon's, veiled by flakes of clouds. She does not care for Ravana's glory. She is brooding over Rama only.

Shlok: राक्षसीभिः परिवृता शोकसंतापकर्शिता।

Translation: मेघलेखापरिवृता चन्द्रलेखेव निष्प्रभा।।5.59.22।।
Chaste Sita of beautiful hips, an auspicious lady though bound is wholly devoted to Rama alone like Sachi, the wife of Indra who was bound by Nahusha.

Shlok: अनुरक्ता हि वैदेही रामं सर्वात्मना शुभा।

Translation: अनन्यचित्ता रामे च पौलोमीव पुरन्दरे।।5.59.24।।
She was like a lustreless lotus in winter. Spurning the advances by Ravana, she is rather determined to commit suicide.
Shlok: अधश्शय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे।।5.59.27।।

Translation: रावणाद्विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया।

To Rama, killing Ravana is easy (since Ravana's power of penance has already declined by his abduction of Sita). Separated from her husband she is naturally emaciated. She has become slender just like a student on the new Moon day (on the first day of study).

Shlok: सा प्रकृत्यैव तन्वङ्गी तद्वियोगाच्च कर्शिता।।  प्रतिपत्पाठशीलस्य विद्येव तनुमतां गता।

Translation: do not deem it fit to be reported there at Kiskindha by you, whose virility is well- known, that the godlike lady Sita has been discovered but not recovered.
Shlok: दृष्टा देवी न चानीता इति तत्र निवेदितुम् ।  न युक्तमिव पश्यामि भवद्भिः ख्यातपौरुषैः ॥

Translation: This suggestion of yours, the way in which you are thinking, O prince, is not at all such as we may not be able to carry out. But devise you the means to accomplish our purpose according to the decision arrived at by Sri Rama.
Shlok: न तावदेषा मतिरक्षमा नो यथा भवान् पश्यति राजपुत्र। यथा तु रामस्य मतिर्निविष्टा तथा भवान् पश्यतु कार्यसिद्धिम् ॥

Translation: Thereafter led by Hanuman, all the vanaras left Mahendra mountain and marched very happily. The vanaras were strong and huge like elephants and resembled mountain Meru. Moreover when they leaped up they seemed to cover the sky.
Shlok: मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशा मत्ता इव महागजाः।  छादयन्त इवाकाशं महाकाया महाबलाः।।

Translation: They were looking at Hanuman without blinking their eyes, and seemed as though they were carrying him by their eyes. They were determined in their minds to please Rama.
Shlok: सभाज्यमानं भूतैस्तमात्मवन्तं महाबलम्।  हनूमन्तं महावेगं वहन्त इव दृष्टिभिः।।

Translation: The monkeys leaped into the sky and entered the garden that resembled the garden of Indra filled with trees and creepers.
Shlok: प्लवमानाः खमाप्लुत्य ततस्ते काननौकसः।  नन्दनोपमयासेदुर्वनं द्रुमलतायुतम्।।

Translation: The vanaras praised Angada, the bull among vanaras and went to Madhuvanam swiftly like a fastflowing river going to uproot a tree.

Shlok: जग्मुर्मधुवनं यत्र नदीवेग इव द्रुमम्।  ते प्रविष्टा मधुवनं पालानाक्रम्य वीर्यतः।।

Translation: shall act as you all will conjointly ask me, O bulls among monkeys; for | depend on you in the matter of deciding what should be done by me.
Shlok: सर्वे यथा मां वक्ष्यन्ति समेत्य हरियूथपाः।  तथास्मि कर्ता कर्तव्ये भवद्भिः परवानहम्।।

Translation: All the vanara troops sprang up into the air as though there was no sky, like stones shattered by machines from the mountains rise up.

Shlok: उत्पतन्तमनूत्पेतु स्सर्वे ते हरियूथपाः।  कृत्वाकाशं निराकाशं यन्त्रोत्क्षिप्ता इवाचलाः।।

Translation: The swift monkeys roared aloud as though they went up the sky like thundering clouds driven by the wind.
Shlok: विनदन्तो महानादं घना वातेरिता यथा।। अङ्गदे ह्यननुप्राप्ते सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः।

Translation: On hearing the nectarlike words from Hanuman that Sita was found, Rama and Lakshmana were delighted.
Shlok: दृष्टा देवीति हनुमद्वदनादमृतोपमम्।।  आकर्ण्य वचनं रामो हर्षमाप सलक्ष्मणः।

Translation: She stretches herself on the bare ground, is pale of limbs like a lotus plant at the approach of winter, has utterly refused to have anything to do with Ravana, and is determined to die rather than submit to Ravana.
Shlok: अधःशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे।  रावणाद्विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया।।5.65.15।।

Translation: The way in which an incident connected with a crow took place in your presence at Citrakuta was also related by her by way of a token, O Sri Rama, exceptionally sagacious scion of Raghu !
Shlok: अभिज्ञानं च मे दत्तं यथा वृत्तं तवान्तिके।

Translation: चित्रकूटे महाप्राज्ञ वायसं प्रति राघव।।5.65.20।।
O sinless one tell Rama that this auspicious Chudamani born in the ocean is sent to him and I was gazing at it as if it was him (Rama) and feeling happy.

Shlok: एष निर्यातितश्श्रीमान्मया ते वारि सम्भवः।

Translation: एतं दृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्यामि व्यसने त्वामिवानघ।।5.65.24।।
With her limbs emaciated through austerities detained in Ravana's inner palace, eyes wide open in fear, Sita said this to me:
Shlok: इति मामब्रवीत्सीता कृशाङ्गी धर्मचारिणी।।5.65.26।।

Translation: रावणान्तः पुरे रुद्धा मृगीवोत्फुल्ललोचना।

By seeing this excellent jewel | have indirectly obtained today the sight of my father in whose hands the jewel was placed by Janaka as well as that of the mighty Janaka, the ruler of the Videha territory, in the same way as | have obtained the sight of Sita herself, O gentle one !
Shlok: इमं दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं यथा तातस्य दर्शनम्।

Translation: अद्यास्म्यवगतस्सौम्य वैदेहस्य तथा विभोः।।5.66.6।।
This jewel was shining on the head of my beloved. Now its mere look makes me feel that I am seeing her.
Shlok: अयं हि शोभते तस्याः प्रियाया मूर्ध्नि मे मणिः।

Translation: अस्याद्य दर्शने नाहं प्राप्तां तामिव चिन्तये।।5.66.7।।
O handsome Hanuman Sita is like water for a thirsty person. Tell me again and again what Sita said to you. Sprinkle on me (lifegiving) water of her words in the form of message.

Shlok: किमाह सीता वैदेही ब्रूहि सौम्य पुनः पुनः।

Translation: पिपासुमिव तोयेन सिञ्चन्ती वाक्यवारिणा।।5.66.8।।
Her face resembling the autumnal Moon bereft of its stain, though covered with rainclouds does not shine so bright.
Shlok: शारद स्तिमिरोन्मुक्तो नूनं चन्द्रं इवांबुधैः।

Translation: आवृतं वदनं तस्या न विराजति राक्षसैः।।5.66.13।।
O Hanuman Tell me now truly what has been told by her. I am eager to know. Indeed, it will keep me alive just as medicne does. (I shall survive on the strength of her message)

Shlok: किमाह सीता हनुमंस्तत्त्वतः कथयाद्य मे।

Translation: एतेन खलु जीविष्ये भेषजेनातुरो यथा।।5.66.14।।
Seeing the blood flowing from her breasts you became furious like a hissing serpent and said:

Shlok: तां तु दृष्ट्वा महाबाहो दारितां च स्तनान्तरे।

Translation: आशीविष इव क्रुद्धो निश्वसन्नभ्यभाषथाः।।5.67.7।।
You took out a blade of grass from your mat and chanted the mantra to invoke the weapon of Brahma (Brahmastra) and hurled it on the crow. It blazed like the fire of the doom's day.

Shlok: स दर्भं संस्तराद्गृह्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण ह्ययोजयः।

Translation: स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्जज्वालाभिमुखः खगम्।।5.67.12।।
Why are the two tigers among men whose power is like that of wind and fire and who are unassailable even to suras are neglecting me?

Shlok: स किमर्थं नरवरो न मां रक्षति राघवः।

Translation: शक्तौ तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ वाय्वग्निसमतेजसौ ।।5.67.22।।
you ought to deliver my message in such a way that the celebrated Sri Rama of mighty arms may deliver me from this ocean of misery.
Shlok: यथा च स महाबाहुर्मा तारयति राघवः ।  अस्मादुःखाम्बुसंरोधात् तत् त्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि ॥5.67.42॥

Translation: This is the message which that noble and self-restrained lady, Sita, gave for you with despondency, O protector of men! Nay, pondering this statement of mine in its true perspective, believe Sita, the foremost of all devoted wives, to be well.
Shlok: एतत् तवार्या नृप संयता सा सीता वचः प्राह विषादपूर्वम् ।  एतच्च बुद्ध्वा गदितं यथा त्वं श्रद्धत्स्व सीतां कुशलां समग्राम् ॥5.67.44॥

Translation: You may appeal to Rama, the son of Dasaratha in many ways, that he should come quickly and slay Ravana in the battle and get me back.

Shlok: एवं बहुविधं वाच्यो रामो दाशरथिस्त्वया।

Translation: यथा मामाप्नुयाच्छीघ्रं हत्वा रावणमाहवे।।5.68.2।।
Tell valiant Rama not to take me back the way Ravana, the demon abducted me out of fear. Which is not right.
Shlok: यथाऽहं तस्य वीरस्य वनादुपधिना हृता।

Translation: रक्षसा तद्भयादेव तथा नार्हति राघवः।।5.68.13।।
There are monkeys who are more powerful than me or equal to me. None are less strong than me or Sugriva.
Shlok: मद्विशिष्टाश्च तुल्याश्च सन्ति तत्र वनौकसः।

Translation: मत्तः प्रत्यवरः कश्चिन्नास्ति सुग्रीवसन्निधौ।।5.68.21।।
O noble lady the lions among men, Rama and Lakshmana who resemble Sun and Moon will ascend on my back and reach here.
Shlok: मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ।

Translation: त्वत्सकाशं महाभागे नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः।।5.68.24।।
You will see the lionlike Rama, a slayer of enemies and Lakshmana wielding bow in hand standing at the entrance of Lanka very soon.
Shlok: अरिघ्नं सिंहसङ्काशं क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्।

Translation: लक्ष्मणं च धनुष्पाणिं लङ्काद्वारमुपस्थितम्।।5.68.25।।
You will hear before long the shouts of generals of the vanaras who resemble rainclouds on the mountain roaring like lions from the Malaya mountain of Lanka.

Shlok: शैलाम्बुदनिकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु।

Translation: नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानामचिराच्छ्रोष्यसि स्वनम्।।5.68.27।।
